title: Animations
text: scene R6 class inherits Scene defines construct(). Inside construct(), self$play() runs one animations time self$wait() holds current frame. self$add() self$remove() change screen instantly, without animation. Named arguments self$play() apply every animation call: run_time: duration seconds (animations default 1). rate_func: function mapping elapsed fraction time, 0 1, fraction animation done. default animations smooth_rate, starts ends slowly. See Rate functions. lag_ratio: much submobjects group staggered. 0 (default animations) move together; 1 starts previous one ends; values overlap. Several animations one self$play() call start together, call lasts long longest . next example plays FadeIn() two rows squares, lag_ratio = 0 lag_ratio = 0.5. Waiting three variants: self$wait(duration) holds frame duration seconds (1 default) updaters keep running. self$pause(duration) holds frozen frame: updaters run, renders faster. self$wait_until(stop_condition, max_time) waits function returns TRUE. covered Updaters value trackers. hood every self$wait() plays Wait() animation, self$play(Wait(1)) self$wait(1).
code: PlayBasics <- R6::R6Class("PlayBasics", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     square <- Square(color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 3)     circle <- Circle(color = RED)$shift(RIGHT * 3)     note <- Text("added without animation", font_size = 28)$to_edge(UP)     self$add(square, note)     self$play(Create(circle), run_time = 1.5, rate_func = linear)     self$remove(note)     self$play(square$animate$shift(RIGHT * 1.5), circle$animate$shift(LEFT * 1.5))     self$wait(0.5)   }) ) LagRatio <- R6::R6Class("LagRatio", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     together <- VGroup(lapply(1:6, function(i) Square(side_length = 0.8, color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.7)))     together$arrange(RIGHT)$shift(UP * 1.2 + RIGHT)     staggered <- together$copy()$set_color(ORANGE)$shift(DOWN * 2.4)     labels <- VGroup(       Text("lag_ratio = 0", font_size = 28)$next_to(together, LEFT, buff = 0.5),       Text("lag_ratio = 0.5", font_size = 28)$next_to(staggered, LEFT, buff = 0.5)     )     self$add(labels)     self$play(FadeIn(together, shift = UP), FadeIn(staggered, shift = UP, lag_ratio = 0.5), run_time = 2)     self$wait(0.5)   }) )

title: Animations
text: Every mobject $animate field. Calling methods records instead applying , result animation morphs mobject current state state calls. Methods can chained, exactly mobject . Animation arguments run_time rate_func can given two places: self$play(), calling $animate like function first method, mob$animate(run_time = 2)$shift(RIGHT). R spelling upstream manim’s mob.animate(run_time=2).shift(RIGHT). Two details keep mind: builder morphs two snapshots. replay method calls frame frame, square$animate$rotate(PI) looks like flip center rather turn. Use Rotate() real rotation. Two builders mobject one self$play() call combine; last one wins. Chain methods single builder instead. default every point travels straight line. path_arc argument makes points travel along arc angle instead; positive angles bend counterclockwise. self$play() accepts builders animation objects alike: converts builders prepare_animation(), can also call , example inspect store animation playing .
code: AnimateBuilder <- R6::R6Class("AnimateBuilder", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     square <- Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5)     self$add(square)     self$play(square$animate$shift(LEFT * 3)$scale(0.5)$set_color(YELLOW))     self$play(square$animate(run_time = 2, rate_func = linear)$shift(RIGHT * 6))     self$play(square$animate$rotate(PI / 4)$set_fill(RED, opacity = 0.8), run_time = 0.75)   }) ) AnimatePathArc <- R6::R6Class("AnimatePathArc", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     straight_path_line <- Line(LEFT * 4 + UP, RIGHT * 4 + UP, color = GREY, stroke_width = 2)     arc_path_line <- ArcBetweenPoints(LEFT * 4 + DOWN, RIGHT * 4 + DOWN, angle = PI / 2, color = GREY, stroke_width = 2)     straight <- Dot(LEFT * 4 + UP, radius = 0.15, color = BLUE)     arced <- Dot(LEFT * 4 + DOWN, radius = 0.15, color = ORANGE)     self$add(straight_path_line, arc_path_line, straight, arced)     self$play(straight$animate$shift(RIGHT * 8), arced$animate(path_arc = PI / 2)$shift(RIGHT * 8), run_time = 2)     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) builder <- Square()$animate$shift(RIGHT)$scale(2) builder #> <animation builder> Square: shift -> scale anim <- prepare_animation(builder) anim #> <MethodAnimation> MethodAnimation(Square) anim$run_time #> [1] 1

title: Animations
text: animations draw mobject onto screen, remove way drawn. “create” style animations add mobject scene start, need call self$add() first. Create() draws outline VMobject along path. DrawBorderThenFill() draws outline, fills . Write() draws submobject’s border fill turn, classic handwriting effect text. run time lag ratio default values based number submobjects; reverse = TRUE writes end. Uncreate() Unwrite() run Create() Write() backwards remove mobject scene finish. SpiralIn() flies submobjects group far away spinning place. scale_factor sets far start. ShowIncreasingSubsets() reveals submobjects group one another keeps ; ShowSubmobjectsOneByOne() shows one time, last one stays end. Text creation animations. glyph Text() submobject, AddTextLetterByLetter() shows one letter time (time_per_char seconds per letter) RemoveTextLetterByLetter() removes way. AddTextWordByWord() takes group whose submobjects words, VGroup Text() objects. TypeWithCursor() types text cursor mobject moves along , UntypeWithCursor() deletes . Blink() (indication animation) makes cursor blink . ShowPartial base class Create() ShowPassingFlash(): moment shows part path two proportions returned get_bounds(alpha) method. Subclass ShowPartialClass define new way revealing path. one grows path middle outward; circle’s middle leftmost point circles start right.
code: CreationBasics <- R6::R6Class("CreationBasics", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     circle <- Circle(color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 4)     square <- Square(color = GREEN, fill_opacity = 0.6)     word <- Text("Write", color = YELLOW)$shift(RIGHT * 4)     self$play(Create(circle))     self$play(DrawBorderThenFill(square), run_time = 1.5)     self$play(Write(word))     self$wait(0.5)   }) ) UncreateUnwrite <- R6::R6Class("UncreateUnwrite", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     circle <- Circle(color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 3)     word <- Text("Unwrite", color = YELLOW)$shift(RIGHT * 3)     note <- Text("Uncreate and Unwrite remove the mobject at the end", font_size = 28)$to_edge(DOWN)     self$add(circle, word, note)     self$wait(0.3)     self$play(Uncreate(circle), Unwrite(word))     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) SpiralInExample <- R6::R6Class("SpiralInExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     shapes <- VGroup(       Circle(radius = 0.8, color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(LEFT * 2.5),       Square(color = GREEN, fill_opacity = 0.5),       Triangle(color = RED, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(RIGHT * 2.5)     )     self$play(SpiralIn(shapes, scale_factor = 3), run_time = 2)     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) Subsets <- R6::R6Class("Subsets", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     top <- VGroup(lapply(1:8, function(i) Dot(radius = 0.2, color = BLUE)))$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.5)$shift(UP)     bottom <- top$copy()$set_color(ORANGE)$shift(DOWN * 2)     self$add(       Text("ShowIncreasingSubsets", font_size = 28)$next_to(top, UP),       Text("ShowSubmobjectsOneByOne", font_size = 28)$next_to(bottom, UP)     )     self$play(ShowIncreasingSubsets(top), ShowSubmobjectsOneByOne(bottom), run_time = 2)     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) LetterByLetter <- R6::R6Class("LetterByLetter", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     first <- Text("AddTextLetterByLetter", font_size = 40)$shift(UP * 1.5)     second <- Text("RemoveTextLetterByLetter", font_size = 40)     words <- VGroup(lapply(c("one", "word", "at", "a", "time"), Text, font_size = 40))     words$arrange(RIGHT, aligned_edge = DOWN)$shift(DOWN * 1.5)     self$play(AddTextLetterByLetter(first, time_per_char = 0.05))     self$add(second)     self$play(RemoveTextLetterByLetter(second, time_per_char = 0.05))     self$play(AddTextWordByWord(words))     self$wait(0.5)   }) ) Typing <- R6::R6Class("Typing", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     text <- Text("Typing", color = PURPLE)$scale(1.5)$to_edge(LEFT)     cursor <- Rectangle(color = GREY_A, fill_color = GREY_A, fill_opacity = 1, height = 1.1, width = 0.5)     cursor$move_to(text[1])     self$play(TypeWithCursor(text, cursor))     self$play(Blink(cursor, blinks = 2, time_on = 0.25, time_off = 0.25))     self$play(UntypeWithCursor(text, cursor))     done <- Text("Done", color = YELLOW)$scale(1.5)$to_edge(LEFT)     self$play(TypeWithCursor(done, cursor))     self$wait(0.5)   }) ) ShowFromMiddle <- R6::R6Class("ShowFromMiddle", inherit = ShowPartialClass,   public = list(     initialize = function(mobject, ...) super$initialize(mobject, introducer = TRUE, ...),     get_bounds = function(alpha) c(0.5 - alpha / 2, 0.5 + alpha / 2)   ) ) ShowPartialExample <- R6::R6Class("ShowPartialExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     line <- Line(LEFT * 5, RIGHT * 5, color = TEAL)$shift(UP * 2)     circle <- Circle(radius = 1.5, color = YELLOW)$shift(DOWN * 0.8)     self$play(ShowFromMiddle$new(line), ShowFromMiddle$new(circle), run_time = 2)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: FadeIn() FadeOut() change opacity, optionally combined movement scale change: shift: vector move along fading (-shift FadeIn(), toward shift FadeOut()). target_position: point mobject fade (FadeIn()) (FadeOut()). scale: scale invisible state, FadeIn(m, scale = 0.2) grows appearing. accept several mobjects , FadeOut(, b, c).
code: Fading <- R6::R6Class("Fading", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     square <- Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(LEFT * 4)     circle <- Circle(color = GREEN, fill_opacity = 0.5)     triangle <- Triangle(color = YELLOW, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(RIGHT * 4)     self$play(FadeIn(square, shift = DOWN), FadeIn(circle, scale = 0.2), FadeIn(triangle, target_position = ORIGIN))     self$play(FadeOut(square, shift = DOWN), FadeOut(triangle, target_position = circle, scale = 0.5))     self$play(FadeIn(Text("FadeIn and FadeOut", font_size = 36)$to_edge(UP), shift = DOWN))     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: Growing animations scale mobject nothing: GrowFromPoint(mobject, point) point (center mobject). GrowFromCenter(mobject) center. GrowFromEdge(mobject, edge) one edges, . GrowArrow(arrow) start arrow, keeping tip shape. SpinInFromNothing(mobject, angle) grows spinning angle. point_color sets color mobject starts .
code: Growing <- R6::R6Class("Growing", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     shapes <- list(       Square(side_length = 1.6, color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5),       Circle(radius = 0.8, color = GREEN, fill_opacity = 0.5),       Rectangle(width = 1, height = 1.8, color = RED, fill_opacity = 0.5),       Arrow(LEFT, RIGHT, color = YELLOW),       Star(outer_radius = 0.9, color = PURPLE, fill_opacity = 0.5)     )     titles <- c("GrowFromPoint", "GrowFromCenter", "GrowFromEdge", "GrowArrow", "SpinInFromNothing")     xs <- c(-5.4, -2.7, 0, 2.7, 5.4)     for (i in seq_along(shapes)) {       shapes[[i]]$move_to(RIGHT * xs[i] + UP * 0.5)       self$add(Text(titles[i], font_size = 20)$move_to(RIGHT * xs[i] + DOWN * 1.2))     }     self$play(       GrowFromPoint(shapes[[1]], ORIGIN),       GrowFromCenter(shapes[[2]]),       GrowFromEdge(shapes[[3]], DOWN),       GrowArrow(shapes[[4]]),       SpinInFromNothing(shapes[[5]], point_color = WHITE),       run_time = 1.5     )     self$wait(0.5)   }) )

title: Animations
text: Indication animations draw attention something without changing good. listed ?indication. Indicate() briefly scales mobject colors (scale_factor, color). Circumscribe() runs frame around , rectangle default circle shape = "circle"; fade_in fade_out fade frame instead drawing . Wiggle() shakes (scale_value, rotation_angle, n_wiggles). ApplyWave() sends wave (direction, amplitude, ripples). second group works points paths: Flash() sends short lines point (num_lines, flash_radius, line_length). FocusOn() shrinks large translucent spotlight onto point. ShowPassingFlash() shows short piece path (time_width, fraction path) traveling along , removes end. ShowPassingFlashWithThinningStrokeWidth() tail gets thinner. Blink() switches opacity mobject (blinks, time_on, time_off, hide_at_end).
code: IndicationText <- R6::R6Class("IndicationText", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     words <- VGroup(lapply(c("Indicate", "Circumscribe", "Wiggle", "ApplyWave"), Text, font_size = 40))     words$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.5)     self$add(words)     self$play(Indicate(words[1]))     self$play(Circumscribe(words[2]))     self$play(Circumscribe(words[2], shape = "circle", fade_out = TRUE, color = BLUE))     self$play(Wiggle(words[3], run_time = 1))     self$play(ApplyWave(words[4], run_time = 1))     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) IndicationPoints <- R6::R6Class("IndicationPoints", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     dot <- Dot(LEFT * 3, radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)     ring <- Circle(radius = 1.2, color = BLUE)$shift(RIGHT * 3)     self$add(dot, ring)     self$play(Flash(dot, flash_radius = 0.3, num_lines = 10))     self$play(FocusOn(dot, run_time = 1))     self$play(ShowPassingFlash(ring$copy()$set_color(YELLOW), time_width = 0.3))     self$play(ShowPassingFlashWithThinningStrokeWidth(ring$copy()$set_stroke(YELLOW, width = 10), time_width = 0.4))     self$play(Blink(dot, blinks = 2, time_on = 0.2, time_off = 0.2))     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: homotopy function point time. Homotopy(homotopy, mobject) takes function function(x, y, z, t) returns new point, applies every point mobject t going 0 1. SmoothedVectorizedHomotopy() smooths curves step, corners round . homotopy moves existing points , give shapes points first insert_n_curves(). ComplexHomotopy() function function(z, t) complex number z = x + iy. PhaseFlow() moves every point along vector field function(p) virtual_time units time. work scene coordinates, homotopy squares point relative center square rather relative origin. flow right shear: points move sideways proportion height. MoveAlongPath(mobject, path) moves mobject center follows path.
code: HomotopyExample <- R6::R6Class("HomotopyExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     wave <- function(x, y, z, t) c(x, y + 0.35 * t * sin(3 * x), z)     word <- Text("Homotopy", font_size = 72)$shift(UP * 1.5)     plain <- Square(side_length = 2, color = BLUE)$insert_n_curves(12)$shift(LEFT * 3 + DOWN * 1.5)     smoothed <- plain$copy()$set_color(ORANGE)$shift(RIGHT * 6)     self$add(word, plain, smoothed)     self$play(Homotopy(wave, word), Homotopy(wave, plain), SmoothedVectorizedHomotopy(wave, smoothed), run_time = 2)     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) FlowExample <- R6::R6Class("FlowExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     center <- -3.5 + 0i     square <- Square(side_length = 2.4, color = BLUE)$insert_n_curves(16)$move_to(c(Re(center), Im(center), 0))     # Squares each point relative to the center of the square, blended in as t grows.     squaring <- function(z, t) {       w <- z - center       center + (1 - t) * w + t * w^2 / 2     }     grid <- VGroup(lapply(1:16, function(i) Square(side_length = 0.6, color = YELLOW)))     grid$arrange_in_grid(4, 4, buff = 0)$shift(RIGHT * 3)     shear <- function(p) c(0.6 * p[2], 0, 0)     self$add(square, grid)     self$play(ComplexHomotopy(squaring, square), PhaseFlow(shear, grid, virtual_time = 1), run_time = 2)     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) MoveAlongPathExample <- R6::R6Class("MoveAlongPathExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     path <- FunctionGraph(function(x) 1.5 * sin(x), x_range = c(-5, 5), color = GREY)     dot <- Dot(path$point_from_proportion(0), radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)     self$add(path, dot)     self$play(MoveAlongPath(dot, path), run_time = 2, rate_func = linear)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: Rotate(mobject, angle) turns mobject angle radians around center, around about_point; points travel along circles, even full turn (angle = TAU) visible. Rotating() spins mobject continuously constant speed (rate_func = linear default) handy many turns; default run time 5 seconds.
code: RotationExample <- R6::R6Class("RotationExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     square <- Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(LEFT * 4)     bar <- Rectangle(width = 2, height = 0.3, color = GREEN, fill_opacity = 0.8)     sun <- Dot(RIGHT * 4, radius = 0.3, color = YELLOW)     planet <- Dot(RIGHT * 4 + UP * 1.5, radius = 0.15, color = TEAL)     self$add(square, bar, sun, planet)     self$play(       Rotate(square, angle = PI / 4),       Rotate(bar, angle = PI / 2, about_point = bar$get_left()),       Rotating(planet, angle = PI, about_point = RIGHT * 4, run_time = 2)     )     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: Transform(, b) morphs shape style b. Two related animations differ screen afterwards: Transform(, b), mobject screen still (now looks like b); b never added. Keep working . ReplacementTransform(, b), gone b screen. Keep working b. TransformFromCopy(, b) leaves place morphs copy b. ClockwiseTransform() CounterclockwiseTransform() Transform() points moving along half circles (path_arc = -pi path_arc = pi).
code: TransformVsReplacement <- R6::R6Class("TransformVsReplacement", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     left_square <- Square(color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 3)     left_circle <- Circle(color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 3)     right_square <- Square(color = ORANGE)$shift(RIGHT * 3)     right_circle <- Circle(color = ORANGE)$shift(RIGHT * 3)     self$add(       Text("Transform", font_size = 28)$move_to(LEFT * 3 + DOWN * 2),       Text("ReplacementTransform", font_size = 28)$move_to(RIGHT * 3 + DOWN * 2),       left_square, right_square     )     self$play(Transform(left_square, left_circle), ReplacementTransform(right_square, right_circle))     # Animate the mobject that is on screen now.     self$play(left_square$animate$set_fill(BLUE, opacity = 0.6), right_circle$animate$set_fill(ORANGE, opacity = 0.6))     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) TransformCopyArcs <- R6::R6Class("TransformCopyArcs", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     source <- Square(side_length = 1, color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(LEFT * 4 + UP * 2.5)     target <- Circle(radius = 0.6, color = GREEN, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(RIGHT * 4 + UP * 2.5)     self$add(source)     self$play(TransformFromCopy(source, target))     a <- Triangle(color = RED)$scale(0.5)$shift(LEFT * 2 + DOWN * 2)     b <- Square(side_length = 0.8, color = RED)$shift(RIGHT * 2 + DOWN * 2)     self$add(a)     self$play(ClockwiseTransform(a, b))     c_shape <- Star(outer_radius = 0.5, color = YELLOW)$shift(RIGHT * 2 + UP * 0.5)     d_shape <- Circle(radius = 0.4, color = YELLOW)$shift(LEFT * 2 + UP * 0.5)     self$add(c_shape)     self$play(CounterclockwiseTransform(c_shape, d_shape))     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: MoveToTarget() works generate_target(): method stores copy mobject mob$target, change copy freely, MoveToTarget(mob) morphs mobject . ApplyMethod() takes method mobject (written without calling , circle$shift) arguments, circle$animate$shift(...) . save_state() stores copy mobject Restore() morphs back . FadeToColor(), ScaleInPlace() ShrinkToCenter() shortcuts recoloring, scaling center, scaling nothing.
code: TargetsAndMethods <- R6::R6Class("TargetsAndMethods", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     circle <- Circle(color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 4)     circle$save_state()     circle$generate_target()     circle$target$shift(RIGHT * 2)$scale(0.5)$set_color(YELLOW)     square <- Square(color = GREEN)$shift(RIGHT * 1.5)     triangle <- Triangle(color = PURPLE)$shift(RIGHT * 4.5)     self$add(circle, square, triangle)     self$play(MoveToTarget(circle))     self$play(ApplyMethod(circle$shift, UP * 1.5))     self$play(Restore(circle))     self$play(FadeToColor(square, RED), ShrinkToCenter(triangle))     self$play(ScaleInPlace(square, 0.5))     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: animations compute target applying function: ApplyFunction(fn, mob): fn receives copy mobject returns modified mobject. ApplyPointwiseFunction(fn, mob): fn maps point (numeric vector c(x, y, z)) new point. ApplyPointwiseFunctionToCenter(fn, mob): moves whole mobject center goes fn(center). ApplyMatrix(matrix, mob): applies 2 x 2 3 x 3 matrix every point, about_point (origin default). ApplyPointwiseFunction() ApplyMatrix() default run time 3 seconds. ApplyComplexFunction(fn, mob) treats point complex number x + iy moves fn(x + iy). Shapes need extra points bend smoothly; NumberPlane gets prepare_for_nonlinear_transform().
code: ApplyFunctions <- R6::R6Class("ApplyFunctions", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     places <- list(LEFT * 3.5 + UP * 1.6, RIGHT * 3.5 + UP * 1.6, LEFT * 3.5 + DOWN * 2, RIGHT * 3.5 + DOWN * 2)     titles <- c("ApplyFunction", "ApplyPointwiseFunction", "ApplyPointwiseFunctionToCenter", "ApplyMatrix")     shapes <- lapply(1:4, function(i) Square(side_length = 1.5, color = BLUE)$insert_n_curves(8)$move_to(places[[i]]))     for (i in 1:4) self$add(shapes[[i]], Text(titles[i], font_size = 24)$next_to(shapes[[i]], UP))     self$play(ApplyFunction(function(m) m$scale(0.6)$rotate(PI / 4)$set_color(YELLOW), shapes[[1]]))     self$play(ApplyPointwiseFunction(function(p) p + c(0, 0.25 * sin(3 * p[1]), 0), shapes[[2]], run_time = 1.5))     self$play(ApplyPointwiseFunctionToCenter(function(p) p + RIGHT * 1.5, shapes[[3]]))     shear <- matrix(c(1, 0, 1, 1), nrow = 2)     self$play(ApplyMatrix(shear, shapes[[4]], about_point = shapes[[4]]$get_center(), run_time = 1.5))     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) ApplyComplex <- R6::R6Class("ApplyComplex", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     plane <- NumberPlane(x_range = c(-1, 1, 0.25), y_range = c(-1.5, 1.5, 0.25))     plane$prepare_for_nonlinear_transform()     self$add(plane)     self$play(ApplyComplexFunction(exp, plane), run_time = 2)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: CyclicReplace(, b, c) moves mobject position next one, last first; Swap(, b) two. move along arcs (path_arc = 90 * DEGREES default). FadeTransform(, b) cross fades instead morphing points: fades stretching shape b, b fades shape . FadeTransformPieces() submobject submobject.
code: SwapAndFade <- R6::R6Class("SwapAndFade", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     shapes <- VGroup(Square(color = BLUE), Circle(color = GREEN), Triangle(color = RED))     shapes$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 1)$scale(0.6)$shift(UP * 2)     self$add(shapes)     self$play(CyclicReplace(shapes[1], shapes[2], shapes[3]))     self$play(Swap(shapes[1], shapes[3]))     one <- VGroup(Square(color = TEAL), Circle(color = TEAL))$arrange(RIGHT)$scale(0.6)$shift(LEFT * 3 + DOWN * 1.5)     two <- VGroup(Triangle(color = ORANGE), Star(color = ORANGE))$arrange(RIGHT)$scale(0.6)$shift(LEFT * 3 + DOWN * 1.5)     three <- one$copy()$shift(RIGHT * 6)     four <- two$copy()$shift(RIGHT * 6)     self$add(one, three)     self$play(FadeTransform(one, two), FadeTransformPieces(three, four), run_time = 1.5)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: TransformMatchingShapes(, b) pairs submobjects shape moves one partner; parts without partner fade . Text() makes anagrams, letter submobject. TransformMatchingTex(, b) MathTex() objects, matching parts LaTeX strings. Split formula parts passing several strings, double braces, "{{}}^2" . Parts move part different string can paired key_map, example key_map = c("+" = "-"). chunk needs LaTeX. accept transform_mismatches = TRUE (morph unmatched parts Transform()) fade_transform_mismatches = TRUE (use FadeTransformPieces() ).
code: MatchingShapes <- R6::R6Class("MatchingShapes", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     source <- Text("the morse code", font_size = 60)     target <- Text("here come dots", font_size = 60)     self$play(Write(source))     self$play(TransformMatchingShapes(source, target, path_arc = PI / 2), run_time = 1.5)     self$wait(0.5)   }) ) MatchingTex <- R6::R6Class("MatchingTex", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     eq1 <- MathTex("{{a}}^2", "+", "{{b}}^2", "=", "{{c}}^2", font_size = 72)     eq2 <- MathTex("{{a}}^2", "=", "{{c}}^2", "-", "{{b}}^2", font_size = 72)     self$add(eq1)     self$wait(0.3)     self$play(TransformMatchingTex(eq1, eq2, key_map = c("+" = "-")), run_time = 1.5)     self$wait(0.5)   }) )

title: Animations
text: Four helpers combine animations one: AnimationGroup(...) plays animations together; lag_ratio, one starts fraction previous one’s run time. Succession(...) plays one another (AnimationGroup() lag_ratio = 1). LaggedStart(...) AnimationGroup() small default lag_ratio 0.05. LaggedStartMap(animation_class, group, ...) applies animation constructor every submobject group, passing remaining named arguments , staggers results. take animations lists animations, lapply() output can passed directly. composed animation can nested another, run_time rate_func apply whole schedule. Wait() Add() useful inside Succession(): Wait(t) nothing t seconds Add(mob) puts mobjects screen instantly point schedule. Broadcast(mob) sends expanding copies mobject focal_point (n_mobs copies, 3 seconds default) removes end.
code: Composition <- R6::R6Class("Composition", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     rows <- lapply(1:4, function(i) {       VGroup(lapply(1:6, function(j) Square(side_length = 0.6, color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.6)))$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.2)     })     VGroup(rows)$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.5)$shift(RIGHT * 2)     titles <- c("AnimationGroup", "Succession", "LaggedStart", "LaggedStartMap")     for (i in 1:4) self$add(Text(titles[i], font_size = 28)$next_to(rows[[i]], LEFT, buff = 0.6))     self$play(AnimationGroup(lapply(rows[[1]]$submobjects, GrowFromCenter), lag_ratio = 0.3))     self$play(Succession(lapply(rows[[2]]$submobjects, function(m) FadeIn(m, run_time = 0.2))))     self$play(LaggedStart(lapply(rows[[3]]$submobjects, function(m) FadeIn(m, shift = DOWN)), lag_ratio = 0.25))     self$play(LaggedStartMap(FadeIn, rows[[4]], shift = UP, lag_ratio = 0.25, run_time = 1))     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) WaitAddBroadcast <- R6::R6Class("WaitAddBroadcast", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     circle <- Circle(color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 4)     square <- Square(color = GREEN)$shift(RIGHT * 4)     self$play(Succession(Add(circle), Wait(0.5), Create(square)))     self$play(Broadcast(Circle(radius = 2, color = YELLOW), n_mobs = 4, run_time = 2))     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: ChangeDecimalToValue(decimal, value) counts DecimalNumber() new value, ChangingDecimal(decimal, fn) sets fn(alpha) animation progresses alpha = 0 alpha = 1. DecimalNumber() typesets digits MathTex() default; mob_class = Text uses system fonts instead, example need LaTeX. Number labels follow moving value usually built updaters instead; see Updaters value trackers.
code: NumberAnimations <- R6::R6Class("NumberAnimations", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     counter <- DecimalNumber(0, num_decimal_places = 1, mob_class = Text, font_size = 96)     self$add(counter)     self$play(ChangeDecimalToValue(counter, 100), run_time = 2)     self$play(ChangingDecimal(counter, function(alpha) 100 - 50 * alpha^2), run_time = 1.5)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: ChangeSpeed(anim, speedinfo) plays animation (builder) varying speed. speedinfo named vector: names points animation, fractions 0 1, values speed factors . two points speed changes smoothly, run time stretches shrinks match. Updaters normally ignore speed changes. updater added change_speed_add_updater() instead mob$add_updater() follows speed playing ChangeSpeed() animation, orange dot slows together blue one. ChangeSpeedClass$add_updater() function name used upstream manim.
code: ChangeSpeedExample <- R6::R6Class("ChangeSpeedExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     a <- Dot(LEFT * 5 + UP, radius = 0.15, color = BLUE)     b <- Dot(LEFT * 5 + DOWN, radius = 0.15, color = ORANGE)     self$add(a, b)     # The updater stops the dot at x = 5, where the blue dot ends.     change_speed_add_updater(b, function(m, dt) m$set_x(min(m$get_x() + 10 * dt, 5)))     self$play(ChangeSpeed(       a$animate$shift(RIGHT * 10),       speedinfo = c("0.3" = 1, "0.4" = 0.1, "0.6" = 0.1, "1" = 1),       rate_func = linear     ))     b$clear_updaters()     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: rate function maps time t [0, 1] progress, also mostly [0, 1]. manimR upstream manim’s rate functions (see ?rate_funcs); upstream’s smooth called smooth_rate R mask stats::smooth(). Utilities vignette shows gallery . plain R functions single number:  function t works rate function, two helpers build new ones old: squish_rate_func(f, , b) runs f times b , not_quite_there(f, proportion) stops short.
code: t <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 101) funs <- list(linear = linear, smooth_rate = smooth_rate, rush_into = rush_into,              there_and_back = there_and_back, ease_out_bounce = ease_out_bounce) values <- sapply(funs, function(f) vapply(t, f, numeric(1))) op <- par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1)) matplot(t, values, type = "l", lty = 1, lwd = 2, xlab = "t", ylab = "rate_func(t)") legend("topleft", names(funs), col = 1:5, lty = 1, lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.8) par(op) RateFunctions <- R6::R6Class("RateFunctions", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     funs <- list(       linear = linear,       smooth_rate = smooth_rate,       rush_from = rush_from,       there_and_back = there_and_back,       ease_out_bounce = ease_out_bounce,       "squish_rate_func(smooth_rate, 0.4, 1)" = squish_rate_func(smooth_rate, 0.4, 1),       "function(t) t^3" = function(t) t^3     )     ys <- seq(3, -3, length.out = length(funs))     dots <- lapply(seq_along(funs), function(i) Dot(c(-0.5, ys[i], 0), color = YELLOW))     for (i in seq_along(funs)) {       self$add(Text(names(funs)[i], font_size = 22)$next_to(c(-0.8, ys[i], 0), LEFT), dots[[i]])     }     self$play(lapply(seq_along(funs), function(i) dots[[i]]$animate(rate_func = funs[[i]])$shift(RIGHT * 6)), run_time = 2)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: transform runs, path function decides route point takes start end. Pass one path_func Transform() relatives ($animate), use path_arc shortcut shown earlier, builds path_along_arc(path_arc) . available path functions (see ?paths) : straight_path(): default. path_along_arc(arc_angle, axis): along arc arc_angle radians. clockwise_path() counterclockwise_path(): half circles. spiral_path(angle): travel direction turns angle way, shape also rotates. path_along_circles(arc_angle, circles_centers): around fixed centers, Rotate() uses. path function R function function(start_points, end_points, alpha) returns interpolated points (n x 3 matrices), can call one directly, write . point traveling (-1, 0) (1, 0) halfway along path:
code: PathFunctions <- R6::R6Class("PathFunctions", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     labels <- c("straight_path()", "path_along_arc(PI / 2)", "spiral_path(-PI / 2)")     ys <- c(2.5, 0, -2.5)     starts <- lapply(ys, function(y) Square(side_length = 0.8, color = BLUE)$move_to(c(-3, y, 0)))     ends <- lapply(ys, function(y) Square(side_length = 0.8, color = ORANGE)$rotate(PI / 4)$move_to(c(3, y, 0)))     for (i in 1:3) self$add(starts[[i]], Text(labels[i], font_size = 22)$next_to(c(-4, ys[i], 0), LEFT))     self$play(Transform(starts[[1]], ends[[1]], path_func = straight_path()))     self$play(Transform(starts[[2]], ends[[2]], path_func = path_along_arc(PI / 2)))     self$play(Transform(starts[[3]], ends[[3]], path_func = spiral_path(-PI / 2)))     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) start <- matrix(c(-1, 0, 0), nrow = 1) end <- matrix(c(1, 0, 0), nrow = 1) path_list <- list(   straight = straight_path(),   arc = path_along_arc(PI / 2),   clockwise = clockwise_path(),   counterclockwise = counterclockwise_path(),   spiral = spiral_path(PI / 2),   circles = path_along_circles(PI / 2, ORIGIN) ) halfway <- t(sapply(path_list, function(f) f(start, end, 0.5))) colnames(halfway) <- c("x", "y", "z") round(halfway, 3) #>                       x      y z #> straight          0.000  0.000 0 #> arc               0.000 -0.414 0 #> clockwise         0.000  1.000 0 #> counterclockwise  0.000 -1.000 0 #> spiral           -0.293 -0.707 0 #> circles           0.000 -0.707 0

title: Animations
text: set_default() changes default arguments mobject animation class every later call, set_default(cls) arguments restores original defaults. scene makes every FadeIn() rise every Create() last two seconds, resets construct() exits. MobjectClass$set_default() AnimationClass$set_default() two base classes, upstream manim.
code: SetDefaultExample <- R6::R6Class("SetDefaultExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     set_default(FadeIn, shift = UP)     set_default(Create, run_time = 2)     on.exit({       set_default(FadeIn)       set_default(Create)     })     self$play(FadeIn(Square(color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 3)))     self$play(Create(Circle(color = GREEN)$shift(RIGHT * 3)))     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: mobject class can decide standard animation looks objects. override_animation(class, "FadeIn", fn) makes FadeIn(obj) call fn(...) method obj (self available) play whatever returns. R form upstream’s @override_animation decorator. Pass use_override = FALSE get normal animation. override_animate(class, "method", fn) customizes obj$animate$method(), like upstream’s @override_animate. function receives method’s arguments plus anim_args, arguments given $animate(...), returns animation. clearing content circle uncreates content, instead default morph. functions change class place, apply every object created afterwards, including objects subclasses. Use classes; overriding built class changes rest R session.
code: Tile <- R6::R6Class("Tile", inherit = SquareClass, lock_objects = FALSE) override_animation(Tile, "FadeIn", function(...) SpinInFromNothing(self, angle = PI, ...)) OverrideAnimationExample <- R6::R6Class("OverrideAnimationExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     tile <- Tile$new(color = YELLOW, fill_opacity = 0.6)$shift(LEFT * 2.5)     plain <- Tile$new(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.6)$shift(RIGHT * 2.5)     self$play(FadeIn(tile), FadeIn(plain, use_override = FALSE), run_time = 1.5)     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) CircleWithContent <- R6::R6Class("CircleWithContent", inherit = VGroupClass, lock_objects = FALSE,   public = list(     circle = NULL,     content = NULL,     initialize = function(content) {       super$initialize()       self$circle <- Circle(color = BLUE)       self$content <- content       self$add(self$circle, content)       content$move_to(self$circle$get_center())     },     clear_content = function() {       self$remove(self$content)       self$content <- NULL       invisible(self)     }   ) ) override_animate(CircleWithContent, "clear_content", function(anim_args = list()) {   anim <- do.call(Uncreate, c(list(self$content), anim_args))   self$clear_content()   anim }) OverrideAnimateExample <- R6::R6Class("OverrideAnimateExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     holder <- CircleWithContent$new(Square(side_length = 1, color = YELLOW))     self$add(holder)     self$wait(0.3)     self$play(holder$animate(run_time = 1.5)$clear_content())     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Animations
text: animation R6 class inherits AnimationClass (generator behind Animation()). playing scene calls three methods: begin() start. default stores copy mobject self$starting_mobject calls interpolate(0). interpolate_mobject(alpha) every frame, alpha going 0 1 linear time. Apply self$rate_func(alpha) override method; default implementation calls interpolate_submobject() submobject staggered alpha (lag_ratio comes ). finish() end. default calls interpolate(1). animation grows mobject nothing spins fades white color. begin() remembers color first frame, finish() gives result thicker outline. introducer = TRUE adds mobject scene animation starts, Create() . Create animation SpinIn$new(...), wrap function spin_in <- function(mobject, ...) SpinIn$new(mobject, ...) get calling style built constructors. Arguments handle (run_time, rate_func, lag_ratio ) pass ... AnimationClass, arguments self$play() reach animation usual.
code: SpinIn <- R6::R6Class("SpinIn", inherit = AnimationClass,   public = list(     angle = TAU,     color = NULL,     initialize = function(mobject, angle = TAU, ...) {       self$angle <- angle       super$initialize(mobject, introducer = TRUE, ...)     },     begin = function() {       self$color <- self$mobject$get_color()       super$begin()     },     interpolate_mobject = function(alpha) {       a <- self$rate_func(alpha)       self$mobject$become(self$starting_mobject)       self$mobject$scale(max(a, 0.001))       self$mobject$rotate(a * self$angle)       self$mobject$set_color(interpolate_color(WHITE, self$color, a))     },     finish = function() {       super$finish()       self$mobject$set_stroke(width = 8)     }   ) ) CustomAnimation <- R6::R6Class("CustomAnimation", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     square <- Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(LEFT * 2.5)     star <- Star(color = YELLOW, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(RIGHT * 2.5)     self$play(SpinIn$new(square), SpinIn$new(star, angle = -PI), run_time = 1.5)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Cameras and 3D scenes
text: size picture visible region configuration settings. Set session manim_config(), one render render(), chunks document knitr::opts_chunk$set(): values can given camera single scene class overriding initialize(): arguments scene use passed camera. also way set background_image, PNG file array values 0 1 replaces background color (drawn pixel pixel top left corner, manim): Inside construct(), self$camera$set_background(pixel_array) self$camera$set_background_from_func(f) replace background image computed R. f receives coordinates c(x, y) pixel returns color c(red, green, blue, alpha) 0 1; called per pixel, takes moment high quality.
code: manim_config(background_color = "#1C1C2E")     # every scene from now on render(MyScene, quality = "m", background_color = WHITE, frame_rate = 24) render(MyScene, pixel_width = 1080, pixel_height = 1080)  # a square video BackgroundImage <- R6::R6Class("BackgroundImage", inherit = Scene,   public = list(     initialize = function(...) {       h <- config$pixel_height       w <- config$pixel_width       shade <- matrix(seq(0.35, 0, length.out = h), h, w)       sky <- array(c(shade * 0.4, shade * 0.6, shade + 0.15), c(h, w, 3))       super$initialize(background_image = sky, ...)     },     construct = function() {       moon <- Circle(radius = 1, color = YELLOW_A)$set_fill(YELLOW_A, opacity = 1)$shift(3 * RIGHT + 1.5 * UP)       set.seed(4)       stars <- VGroup(lapply(1:40, function(i) Dot(c(runif(1, -7, 7), runif(1, -4, 4), 0), radius = 0.025)))       self$add(stars)       self$play(FadeIn(moon, shift = DOWN), run_time = 1.5)     }   ) ) RadialBackground <- R6::R6Class("RadialBackground", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     self$camera$set_background_from_func(function(xy) {       r <- min(sqrt(sum(xy^2)) / 8, 1)       c(0.15 * (1 - r), 0.1 + 0.25 * (1 - r), 0.05 + 0.35 * (1 - r), 1)     })     square <- Square(side_length = 3, color = WHITE)$set_fill(ORANGE, opacity = 0.8)     self$play(DrawBorderThenFill(square), run_time = 1.5)   }) )

title: Cameras and 3D scenes
text: MovingCameraScene MovingCameraClass camera whose visible region rectangle mobject, self$camera$frame. Moving, scaling animating frame pans zooms; everything else scene stays . frame ordinary mobject, save_state() Restore() work . self$camera$frame$animate$set(width = 4) sets visible width directly, camera methods get_frame_width(), get_frame_height(), get_frame_center(), set_frame_width(), set_frame_height() set_frame_center() read change frame without animation. is_in_frame(mob) tells whether mobject least partly visible.
code: ZoomInOut <- R6::R6Class("ZoomInOut", inherit = MovingCameraScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     square <- Square(side_length = 3, color = BLUE)$set_fill(BLUE, opacity = 0.3)     dot <- Dot(square$get_corner(UR), color = YELLOW)     self$add(square, dot)     self$camera$frame$save_state()     self$play(self$camera$frame$animate$scale(0.4)$move_to(dot), run_time = 1.5)     self$play(dot$animate$shift(0.5 * LEFT), run_time = 0.8)     self$play(Restore(self$camera$frame), run_time = 1.5)   }) )

title: Cameras and 3D scenes
text: updater frame makes camera follow moving mobject. upstream’s classic example: camera zooms dot, rides along graph , zooms .
code: FollowingGraphCamera <- R6::R6Class("FollowingGraphCamera", inherit = MovingCameraScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     self$camera$frame$save_state()     ax <- Axes(x_range = c(-1, 10), y_range = c(-1, 10))     graph <- ax$plot(function(x) sin(x), color = BLUE, x_range = c(0, 3 * PI))     moving_dot <- Dot(ax$i2gp(graph$t_min, graph), color = ORANGE)     dot_1 <- Dot(ax$i2gp(graph$t_min, graph))     dot_2 <- Dot(ax$i2gp(graph$t_max, graph))     self$add(ax, graph, dot_1, dot_2, moving_dot)     self$play(self$camera$frame$animate$scale(0.5)$move_to(moving_dot), run_time = 1)     follow <- function(mob) mob$move_to(moving_dot$get_center())     self$camera$frame$add_updater(follow)     self$play(MoveAlongPath(moving_dot, graph, rate_func = linear), run_time = 2)     self$camera$frame$remove_updater(follow)     self$play(Restore(self$camera$frame), run_time = 1)   }) )

title: Cameras and 3D scenes
text: self$camera$auto_zoom(mobjects, margin) returns animation moves scales frame mobjects just fit, plus margin. animate = FALSE moves frame instead, only_mobjects_in_frame = TRUE ignores mobjects screen.
code: AutoZoom <- R6::R6Class("AutoZoom", inherit = MovingCameraScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     small <- VGroup(Square(side_length = 0.6, color = RED), Circle(radius = 0.3, color = YELLOW))     small$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.3)$shift(4 * LEFT + 2 * DOWN)     big <- Star(color = BLUE)$scale(1.5)$shift(3 * RIGHT + UP)     self$add(small, big)     self$play(self$camera$auto_zoom(small, margin = 0.5), run_time = 1.5)     self$play(self$camera$auto_zoom(list(small, big), margin = 1), run_time = 1.5)   }) )

title: Cameras and 3D scenes
text: ZoomedScene adds second camera, self$zoomed_camera, whose view shown inset, self$zoomed_display. zoomed camera’s frame (rectangle scene) marks magnified. activate_zooming() turns (animate = TRUE also plays zoom pop animations); get_zoomed_display_pop_out_animation() animates display growing frame. settings arguments scene’s initialize(), scene wants values overrides : zoom_factor (size zoomed frame relative display, 0.15 default), zoomed_display_height, zoomed_display_width, zoomed_display_center zoomed_display_corner, zoomed_display_corner_buff, image_frame_stroke_width, zoomed_camera_frame_starting_position, zoomed_camera_config (arguments zoomed MovingCameraClass) zoomed_camera_image_mobject_config. shortened version upstream’s MovingZoomedSceneAround: get_zoom_factor() returns current magnification ratio get_zoom_in_animation() animation activate_zooming(animate = TRUE) plays first. zoomed display ImageMobjectFromCamera(), drawn scene’s MultiCameraClass camera. can build picture picture hand MovingCameraScene uses MultiCameraClass camera: MultiCameraClass$new(image_mobjects_from_cameras, allow_cameras_to_capture_their_own_display) camera; add_image_mobject_from_camera() registers displays later.
code: MovingZoomedSceneAround <- R6::R6Class("MovingZoomedSceneAround", inherit = ZoomedScene,   public = list(     initialize = function(...) {       super$initialize(zoom_factor = 0.3, zoomed_display_height = 1, zoomed_display_width = 6,                        image_frame_stroke_width = 20,                        zoomed_camera_config = list(default_frame_stroke_width = 3), ...)     },     construct = function() {       dot <- Dot()$shift(UL * 2)       image <- ImageMobject(matrix(c(0, 100, 30, 200, 255, 0, 5, 33), 2, byrow = TRUE))       image$height <- 7       frame_text <- Text("Frame", color = PURPLE, font_size = 67)       zoomed_camera_text <- Text("Zoomed camera", color = RED, font_size = 67)       self$add(image, dot)       frame <- self$zoomed_camera$frame       zoomed_display <- self$zoomed_display       zoomed_display_frame <- zoomed_display$display_frame       frame$move_to(dot)       frame$set_color(PURPLE)       zoomed_display_frame$set_color(RED)       zoomed_display$shift(DOWN)       zd_rect <- BackgroundRectangle(zoomed_display, fill_opacity = 0, buff = MED_SMALL_BUFF)       self$add_foreground_mobject(zd_rect)       unfold_camera <- UpdateFromFunc(zd_rect, function(rect) rect$replace(zoomed_display))       frame_text$next_to(frame, DOWN)       self$play(Create(frame), FadeIn(frame_text, shift = UP), run_time = 1)       self$activate_zooming()       self$play(self$get_zoomed_display_pop_out_animation(), unfold_camera, run_time = 1)       zoomed_camera_text$next_to(zoomed_display_frame, DOWN)       self$play(FadeIn(zoomed_camera_text, shift = UP), FadeOut(frame_text), run_time = 0.8)       self$play(frame$animate$shift(2.5 * DOWN), FadeOut(zoomed_camera_text), run_time = 1.5)     }   ) ) PictureInPicture <- R6::R6Class("PictureInPicture", inherit = MovingCameraScene,   public = list(     default_camera_class = function() MultiCameraClass,     construct = function() {       grid <- NumberPlane()       target <- Star(color = YELLOW)$scale(0.4)$shift(2 * LEFT + DOWN)       self$add(grid, target)       inset_camera <- MovingCameraClass$new(default_frame_stroke_width = 3)       inset_camera$frame$set(height = 2)$move_to(target)       inset <- ImageMobjectFromCamera(inset_camera)       inset$add_display_frame()       inset$set(height = 3)$to_corner(UR)       self$camera$add_image_mobject_from_camera(inset)       self$add(inset_camera$frame, inset)       self$play(Rotate(target, angle = PI), run_time = 1.5)     }   ) )

title: Cameras and 3D scenes
text: ThreeDScene looks scene point sphere around frame center: phi polar angle, measured z axis: phi = 0 looks straight (default, 3D scene starts looking like 2D one), phi = 90 * DEGREES looks horizontally; theta azimuth, angle around z axis (-90 * DEGREES default, puts x axis horizontal); gamma rolls camera line sight; zoom magnifies picture; focal_distance sets strength perspective (smaller stronger); frame_center 3D point center screen. set_camera_orientation() sets . Angles radians; multiply degrees DEGREES.
code: CameraOrientation <- R6::R6Class("CameraOrientation", inherit = ThreeDScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     axes <- ThreeDAxes()     cube <- Cube(side_length = 2, fill_color = BLUE)$shift(OUT)     self$set_camera_orientation(phi = 70 * DEGREES, theta = -40 * DEGREES, zoom = 0.9)     self$add(axes, cube)   }) )

title: Cameras and 3D scenes
text: Titles labels usually rotated scene. add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects() pins mobjects screen, drawn camera lens. add_fixed_orientation_mobjects() keeps mobjects facing viewer position follows 3D scene, suits axis labels. remove_fixed_in_frame_mobjects() remove_fixed_orientation_mobjects() undo .
code: FixedInFrameMObjectTest <- R6::R6Class("FixedInFrameMObjectTest", inherit = ThreeDScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     axes <- ThreeDAxes()     self$set_camera_orientation(phi = 75 * DEGREES, theta = -45 * DEGREES)     text3d <- Text("This is a 3D text")     self$add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects(text3d)     text3d$to_corner(UL)     x_label <- Text("x", color = YELLOW)$move_to(axes$c2p(6.6, 0, 0))     z_label <- Text("z", color = YELLOW)$move_to(axes$c2p(0.6, 0, 3.6))     self$add_fixed_orientation_mobjects(x_label, z_label)     self$add(axes)     self$begin_ambient_camera_rotation(rate = 0.4)     self$wait(1.5)   }) )

title: Cameras and 3D scenes
text: move_camera() animates camera new angles (phi, theta, gamma, zoom, focal_distance frame_center), together animations added_anims. begin_ambient_camera_rotation(rate, ) keeps turning camera ("theta", "phi" "gamma") stop_ambient_camera_rotation(). upstream’s ThreeDCameraRotation: begin_3dillusion_camera_rotation(rate) wobbles camera small ellipse instead, gives sense depth without turning scene away; stop_3dillusion_camera_rotation() ends . angles live value trackers camera (phi_tracker, theta_tracker, gamma_tracker, zoom_tracker, focal_distance_tracker), read get_phi(), get_theta(), get_gamma(), get_zoom() get_focal_distance() set without animation set_phi(), set_theta(), set_gamma(), set_zoom() set_focal_distance(); scene’s camera_tracker("theta") returns one trackers. project_point(p) gives screen position 3D point current view. Animating tracker , example self$play(self$camera$theta_tracker$animate$set_value(PI)), move_camera().
code: ThreeDCameraRotation <- R6::R6Class("ThreeDCameraRotation", inherit = ThreeDScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     axes <- ThreeDAxes()     circle <- Circle()     self$set_camera_orientation(phi = 75 * DEGREES, theta = 30 * DEGREES)     self$add(circle, axes)     self$begin_ambient_camera_rotation(rate = 0.5)     self$wait(1.5)     self$stop_ambient_camera_rotation()     self$move_camera(phi = 60 * DEGREES, theta = -60 * DEGREES, gamma = 10 * DEGREES, zoom = 1.3,                      run_time = 1.5)   }) ) ThreeDCameraIllusionRotation <- R6::R6Class("ThreeDCameraIllusionRotation", inherit = ThreeDScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     axes <- ThreeDAxes()     circle <- Circle()     self$set_camera_orientation(phi = 75 * DEGREES, theta = 30 * DEGREES)     self$add(circle, axes)     self$begin_3dillusion_camera_rotation(rate = 2)     self$wait(PI / 2)     self$stop_3dillusion_camera_rotation()   }) )

code: ThreeDLightSourcePosition <- R6::R6Class("ThreeDLightSourcePosition", inherit = ThreeDScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     axes <- ThreeDAxes()     sphere <- Surface(       function(u, v) c(1.5 * cos(u) * cos(v), 1.5 * cos(u) * sin(v), 1.5 * sin(u)),       v_range = c(0, TAU), u_range = c(-PI / 2, PI / 2),       checkerboard_colors = c(RED_D, RED_E), resolution = c(15, 32)     )     self$camera$light_source$move_to(3 * IN)     self$set_camera_orientation(phi = 75 * DEGREES, theta = 30 * DEGREES)     self$add(axes, sphere)   }) ) blue <- c(0.2, 0.4, 0.8) get_shaded_rgb(blue, point = ORIGIN, unit_normal_vect = OUT, light_source = 10 * OUT) #> [1] 0.7 0.9 1.3 get_shaded_rgb(blue, point = ORIGIN, unit_normal_vect = IN, light_source = 10 * OUT) #> [1] -0.05  0.15  0.55 FlatLook <- R6::R6Class("FlatLook", inherit = ThreeDScene,   public = list(     initialize = function(...) super$initialize(should_apply_shading = FALSE, ...),     construct = function() self$add(Sphere())   ) )

title: Cameras and 3D scenes
text: Surface(func, u_range, v_range, resolution) draws parametric surface: func(u, v) returns point c(x, y, z). surface made resolution (one number c(u, v)) small faces colored alternately checkerboard_colors; fill_color, fill_opacity, stroke_color stroke_width style . set_fill_by_checkerboard() recolors faces afterwards. upstream’s Gaussian surface:  ThreeDAxes() methods Axes (see Graphs, plots coordinate systems) plus z axis (z_range, z_length, z_axis_config). axes$plot_surface(f, u_range, v_range) draws z = f(x, y) axes’ coordinates, colorscale argument colors faces height (example colorscale = c(BLUE, TEAL, YELLOW, RED)). set_fill_by_value(axes, colorscale, axis) surface; axis 1, 2 3 x, y z, colorscale vector colors spread axis range, list list(color, value) pairs. get_axis_labels() ThreeDAxes also labels z axis.
code: ThreeDSurfacePlot <- R6::R6Class("ThreeDSurfacePlot", inherit = ThreeDScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     self$set_camera_orientation(phi = 75 * DEGREES, theta = -30 * DEGREES)     param_gauss <- function(u, v) {       sigma <- 0.4       c(u, v, exp(-(u^2 + v^2) / (2 * sigma^2)))     }     gauss_plane <- Surface(param_gauss, resolution = c(24, 24), v_range = c(-2, 2), u_range = c(-2, 2))     gauss_plane$scale(2, about_point = ORIGIN)     gauss_plane$set_style(fill_opacity = 1, stroke_color = GREEN)     gauss_plane$set_fill_by_checkerboard(ORANGE, BLUE, opacity = 0.5)     axes <- ThreeDAxes()     self$add(axes, gauss_plane)   }) ) SurfacePlot <- R6::R6Class("SurfacePlot", inherit = ThreeDScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     axes <- ThreeDAxes(x_range = c(-3, 3, 1), y_range = c(-3, 3, 1), z_range = c(-1, 1, 0.5),                        x_length = 6, y_length = 6, z_length = 3)     wave <- axes$plot_surface(function(x, y) sin(x) * cos(y), u_range = c(-3, 3), v_range = c(-3, 3),                               resolution = c(18, 18), fill_opacity = 0.9)     wave$set_fill_by_value(axes = axes, axis = 3,                            colorscale = list(list(BLUE, -1), list(TEAL, -0.3), list(YELLOW, 0.3), list(RED, 1)))     self$set_camera_orientation(phi = 65 * DEGREES, theta = -50 * DEGREES, zoom = 0.9)     self$add(axes, wave)     self$begin_ambient_camera_rotation(rate = 0.3)     self$wait(1.5)   }) )

Sphere(radius = 1, resolution = c(16, 8))$move_to(c(-4.5, 1.8, 0))     cube <- Cube(side_length = 1.5, fill_color = BLUE)$move_to(c(0, 1.8, 0))     prism <- Prism(dimensions = c(2.4, 1.2, 0.8), cone, cylinder, torus)   }) ) Lines3D <- R6::R6Class("Lines3D", inherit = ThreeDScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     self$set_camera_orientation(phi = 70 * DEGREES, theta = -30 * DEGREES)     axes <- ThreeDAxes(x_range = c(-3, 3, 1), y_range = c(-3, 3, 1), z_range = c(-2, 2, 1),                        x_length = 6, y_length = 6, z_length = 4)     line <- Line3D(start = c(-2, -2, -1), end = c(2, 2, 1), color = YELLOW, resolution = 8)     parallel <- Line3D_parallel_to(line, point = c(1, -2, 0), length = 4, color = GREEN, resolution = 8)     perpendicular <- Line3D_perpendicular_to(line, point = c(-2, 1, 1), length = 3, color = RED,                                              resolution = 8)     arrow <- Arrow3D(start = ORIGIN, end = c(0, 0, 2), color = R6::R6Class("ShadedFace", inherit = ThreeDScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     self$set_camera_orientation(phi = 65 * DEGREES, theta = -60 * DEGREES)     corners <- rbind(c(-1, -1, 0), c(1, -1, 0), c(1, 1, 0), c(-1, 1, 0), c(-1, -1, 0))     flat <- VMobject(fill_color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 1)$set_points_as_corners(corners)$shift(2.5 * LEFT)     shaded <- ThreeDVMobject(fill_color = text: Tetrahedron(), Octahedron(), Icosahedron() Dodecahedron() platonic solids, sized edge_length. Polyhedron(vertex_coords, faces_list) builds polyhedron matrix vertices list faces (1 based vertex indices, file format), ConvexHull3D(points) wraps cloud points. faces $faces vertices edges $graph, Graph(); style faces_config graph_config, afterwards fields. vertex small Dot3D() sphere. scene many vertices draws faster coarser ones, set graph_config:
code: PolyhedraGallery <- R6::R6Class("PolyhedraGallery", inherit = ThreeDScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     self$set_camera_orientation(phi = 75 * DEGREES, theta = -80 * DEGREES)     coarse <- list(vertex_config = list(resolution = c(4, 4)))     solids <- list(       Tetrahedron(edge_length = 2, graph_config = coarse),       Octahedron(edge_length = 1.8, graph_config = coarse),       Icosahedron(edge_length = 1.3, graph_config = coarse),       Dodecahedron(edge_length = 0.9, graph_config = coarse)     )     xs <- c(-4.5, -1.5, 1.5, 4.5)     for (k in seq_along(solids)) solids[[k]]$move_to(c(xs[k], 0, 1.6))     solids[[2]]$faces[3]$set_color(YELLOW)     solids[[2]]$graph[1]$set_color(RED)     pyramid <- Polyhedron(       rbind(c(1, 1, 0), c(1, -1, 0), c(-1, -1, 0), c(-1, 1, 0), c(0, 0, 2)),       list(c(1, 2, 5), c(2, 3, 5), c(3, 4, 5), c(4, 1, 5), c(1, 2, 3, 4)),       faces_config = list(fill_color = ORANGE, fill_opacity = 0.7), graph_config = coarse     )$scale(0.8)$move_to(c(-2, 0, -1.8))     set.seed(3)     cloud <- matrix(rnorm(45), ncol = 3)     hull <- ConvexHull3D(cloud, faces_config = list(fill_color = TEAL, fill_opacity = 0.6),                          graph_config = coarse)$scale(0.6)$move_to(c(2, 0, -1.8))     self$add(VGroup(solids), pyramid, hull)   }) )

title: Cameras and 3D scenes
text: LinearTransformationScene sets gray background plane, blue plane top gets transformed, basis vectors hat (green) j hat (red). Mobjects added add_transformable_mobject(), add_vector() add_unit_square() move every transformation; add_background_mobject() add_foreground_mobject() add mobjects stay put. : apply_matrix(m) animates linear map m (2 x 2 R matrix, matrix(c(1, 0, 1, 1), 2) shear columns (1, 0) (1, 1)); apply_transposed_matrix(t_m) takes matrix rows, 3Blue1Brown’s old code ; apply_inverse() apply_inverse_transpose() undo map; apply_nonlinear_transformation(f) apply_function(f) animate function points. takes run_time (3 seconds default) added_anims. Options scene go initialize(): show_basis_vectors, show_coordinates, leave_ghost_vectors (keep faded copies vectors step), include_background_plane, include_foreground_plane, background_plane_kwargs, foreground_plane_kwargs, i_hat_color, j_hat_color basis_vector_stroke_width. basis vectors use colors X_COLOR (green) Y_COLOR (red); Z_COLOR (blue) completes set 3D. get_unit_square(color, opacity, stroke_width) returns unit square without adding , get_matrix_transformation(m) returns map function points, get_ghost_vectors() faded copies. VectorScene simpler base class, helpers draw: add_plane() add_axes(), get_vector(coords) (arrow self$plane), add_vector() (animate = TRUE grows arrow), get_basis_vectors(), label_vector() get_vector_label(), get_basis_vector_labels(), write_vector_coordinates(), animated explanations coords_to_vector() vector_to_coords(), show_ghost_movement(). labels coordinates typeset LaTeX: LinearTransformationScene adds LaTeX labels follow transformations : add_title() writes title foreground, add_transformable_label(vector, label) labels vector rewrites label L(v) transformation applied, add_moving_mobject() moves mobject’s center map. lock_in_faded_grid() draws faded grid camera’s background image, keeps per frame work.
code: Shear <- R6::R6Class("Shear", inherit = LinearTransformationScene,   public = list(     initialize = function(...) super$initialize(leave_ghost_vectors = TRUE, ...),     construct = function() {       self$add_unit_square()       self$add_vector(c(-1, 2), color = YELLOW)       self$add_transformable_mobject(Circle(radius = 0.5, color = PINK)$move_to(c(2, 1, 0)))       self$apply_matrix(matrix(c(1, 0, 1, 1), 2), run_time = 1.5)       # The rotation matrix(c(0, 1, -1, 0), 2), given by rows:       self$apply_transposed_matrix(matrix(c(0, -1, 1, 0), 2), run_time = 1.5)     }   ) ) Warp <- R6::R6Class("Warp", inherit = LinearTransformationScene,   public = list(     initialize = function(...) super$initialize(show_basis_vectors = FALSE, ...),     construct = function() {       self$apply_nonlinear_transformation(function(p) {         p + c(0.3 * sin(p[2]), 0.3 * sin(p[1]), 0)       }, run_time = 2)     }   ) ) VectorCoordinates <- R6::R6Class("VectorCoordinates", inherit = VectorScene,   public = list(construct = function() {     self$plane <- self$add_plane()$fade(0.5)     v <- self$add_vector(c(2, 1), color = YELLOW, animate = FALSE)     self$label_vector(v, "v", animate = FALSE)     self$add(self$get_basis_vectors(), self$get_basis_vector_labels())     self$vector_to_coords(v, clean_up = FALSE)   }) )

code: SplitScreen <- R6::R6Class("SplitScreen", inherit = Scene,   public = list(     initialize = function(...) {       left <- MovingCamera()       right <- MovingCamera()       right$frame$scale(0.35)$move_to(c(2, 1, 0))       super$initialize(camera_class = SplitScreenCameraClass, left_camera = left, right_camera = right, ...)     },     construct = function() {       self$add(NumberPlane(), Circle(radius = 3, color = BLUE), Dot(c(2, 1, 0), color = YELLOW),                Square(side_length = 1, color = RED)$move_to(c(2, 1, 0)))     }   ) ) FourViews <- R6::R6Class("FourViews", inherit = Scene,   public = list(     initialize = function(...) {       w <- config$pixel_width %/% 2       h <- config$pixel_height %/% 2       cams <- lapply(1:4, function(i) MovingCamera(pixel_width = w, pixel_height = h))       cams[[2]]$frame$scale(0.5)$move_to(c(2, 1, 0))       cams[[3]]$frame$scale(0.5)$move_to(c(-2, -1, 0))       super$initialize(camera_class = OldMultiCameraClass, cameras_with_start_positions = list(         list(cams[[1]], c(0, 0)), list(cams[[2]], c(0, w)),         list(cams[[3]], c(h, 0)), list(cams[[4]], c(h, w))       ), ...)     },     construct = function() {       self$add(NumberPlane(), Circle(radius = 3, color = BLUE), Dot(c(2, 1, 0), color = YELLOW),                Dot(c(-2, -1, 0), color = RED))     }   ) )

title: Colors, images, SVG and point clouds
text: standard manim palette comes families five shades, _A (lightest) _E (darkest). name without suffix _C shade: BLUE BLUE_C. Gray spelled ways (GRAY_A GREY_A). draw swatches , small helper uses base graphics. labels swatch black white, whichever contrasts better, using contrasting() method ManimColor.  remaining named colors grays, pure primaries, singles colors manim logo:  LIGHTER_GREY, LIGHT_GREY, GREY, DARK_GREY, DARKER_GREY GREY_BROWN colors British spelling.
code: show_swatches <- function(cols, ncol = 5, cex = 0.7, show_hex = TRUE) {   n <- length(cols)   nrow <- ceiling(n / ncol)   op <- par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))   on.exit(par(op))   plot.new()   plot.window(c(0, ncol), c(0, nrow), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")   i <- seq_len(n) - 1   x <- i %% ncol   y <- nrow - 1 - i %/% ncol   rect(x + 0.03, y + 0.06, x + 0.97, y + 0.94, col = unlist(cols), border = "grey85")   ink <- vapply(cols, function(cl) as.character(ManimColor(cl)$contrasting()), "")   text(x + 0.5, y + if (show_hex) 0.62 else 0.5, names(cols), cex = cex, col = ink)   if (show_hex) text(x + 0.5, y + 0.36, unlist(cols), cex = cex * 0.9, col = ink) } families <- c("BLUE", "TEAL", "GREEN", "YELLOW", "GOLD", "RED", "MAROON", "PURPLE", "GRAY") shades <- unlist(lapply(families, function(f) paste0(f, "_", c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")))) show_swatches(mget(shades, envir = asNamespace("manimR")), ncol = 5) others <- c("WHITE", "LIGHTER_GRAY", "LIGHT_GRAY", "GRAY", "DARK_GRAY", "DARKER_GRAY", "BLACK",             "PURE_RED", "PURE_GREEN", "PURE_BLUE", "PURE_CYAN", "PURE_MAGENTA", "PURE_YELLOW",             "DARK_BLUE", "PINK", "LIGHT_PINK", "ORANGE", "LIGHT_BROWN", "DARK_BROWN", "GRAY_BROWN",             "LOGO_WHITE", "LOGO_GREEN", "LOGO_BLUE", "LOGO_RED", "LOGO_BLACK") show_swatches(mget(others, envir = asNamespace("manimR")), ncol = 7, cex = 0.62)

text: Six larger palettes upstream’s color modules named lists hex strings. Pick color $, XKCD$AVOCADO. X11_COLORS upstream’s X11 (renamed mask grDevices::X11()). X11_COLORS SVGNAMES: X11 SVG named colors. XKCD: color names xkcd color survey. DVIPSNAMES: colors LaTeX’s dvipsnames option. AS2700: Australian standard colors (codes B11_RICH_BLUE). BS381: British standard colors, number (BS381_101) name. Six evenly spaced samples palette:  list color mirrors upstream’s color module, ported code color.X11.BEIGE becomes color$X11$BEIGE:
code: palettes <- list(X11_COLORS = X11_COLORS, XKCD = XKCD, SVGNAMES = SVGNAMES,                  DVIPSNAMES = DVIPSNAMES, AS2700 = AS2700, BS381 = BS381) vapply(palettes, length, integer(1)) #> X11_COLORS       XKCD   SVGNAMES DVIPSNAMES     AS2700      BS381  #>        504        922        151         68        206        287 XKCD$AVOCADO #> [1] "#90B134" SVGNAMES$CORNFLOWERBLUE #> [1] "#6395ED" head(names(AS2700)) #> [1] "B11_RICH_BLUE"   "B12_ROYAL_BLUE"  "B13_NAVY_BLUE"   "B14_SAPHHIRE"    #> [5] "B15_MID_BLUE"    "B21_ULTRAMARINE" head(names(BS381)) #> [1] "BS381_101"      "SKY_BLUE"       "BS381_102"      "TURQUOISE_BLUE" #> [5] "BS381_103"      "PEACOCK_BLUE" samples <- unlist(lapply(names(palettes), function(p) {   pal <- palettes[[p]]   pick <- pal[round(seq(1, length(pal), length.out = 6))]   setNames(pick, paste0(p, "$\n", names(pick))) }), recursive = FALSE) show_swatches(samples, ncol = 6, cex = 0.58, show_hex = FALSE) color$X11$BEIGE #> [1] "#F5F5DC" color$BLUE_C #> [1] "#58C4DD"

title: Colors, images, SVG and point clouds
text: interpolate_color() blends two colors color_gradient() spreads number colors sequence. average_color() averages several colors, invert_color() takes complement, lighter_color() darker_color() blend toward white black. picture shows gradient 24 steps ladder lighter darker versions BLUE.
code: interpolate_color(RED, BLUE, 0.5) #> ManimColor('#AA9399') color_gradient(c(RED, YELLOW, GREEN), 5) #> [1] "#FC6255" "#F99D62" "#F7D96F" "#BDCD6B" "#83C167" average_color(RED, BLUE, GREEN) #> ManimColor('#9DA288') invert_color(RED) #> ManimColor('#029DAA') lighter_color(RED, blend = 0.3) #> ManimColor('#FC9188') darker_color(RED, blend = 0.3) #> ManimColor('#B0443B') bar <- VGroup(lapply(color_gradient(c(BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW, RED), 24), function(cl) {   Rectangle(width = 0.45, height = 1, stroke_width = 0, fill_color = cl, fill_opacity = 1) }))$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0) blends <- c(seq(0.8, 0.2, by = -0.2), 0, seq(0.2, 0.8, by = 0.2)) ladder <- VGroup(lapply(seq_along(blends), function(i) {   cl <- if (i < 5) darker_color(BLUE, blends[i]) else if (i == 5) BLUE else lighter_color(BLUE, blends[i])   Square(side_length = 0.9, stroke_width = 0, fill_color = cl, fill_opacity = 1) }))$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.1) plot(VGroup(bar, ladder)$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.6))

title: Colors, images, SVG and point clouds
text: random_color() picks one manim colors random_bright_color() blends random one halfway white. use R’s random number generator, set.seed() makes repeatable. RandomColorGenerator() stream: seed repeats sequence without touching R’s global seed. next_color() method (also callable gen$`next`(), since next reserved R) returns next color, chosen sample_colors given. generator RandomColorGeneratorClass.
code: set.seed(1) random_color() #> [1] "#9A72AC" random_bright_color() #> ManimColor('#909090') gen <- RandomColorGenerator(seed = 42) c(gen$next_color(), gen$`next`(), gen$next_color()) #> [1] "#E07A5F" "#9A72AC" "#444444" again <- RandomColorGenerator(seed = 42) again$next_color() # the same first color #> ManimColor('#E07A5F') traffic <- RandomColorGenerator(seed = 1, sample_colors = c(RED, YELLOW, GREEN)) replicate(5, traffic$next_color()) #> [1] "#FC6255" "#83C167" "#FC6255" "#F7D96F" "#FC6255"

text: ManimColor() (also called RGBA()) builds upstream’s color object. hex string exact RGBA value attached, works anywhere color , brings upstream’s methods $. accepts names, hex strings (# 0x), integers 0xFF0000, three four channels, either [0, 1] integers 0 255.

title: Colors, images, SVG and point clouds
text: HSV() holds color hue, saturation value. Read set channels $hue, $saturation $value ($h, $s, $v), color updates. HSVClass class methods ManimColorClass. Varying hue gives quick rainbow:
code: h <- HSV(c(0.25, 1, 1)) h #> HSV('#7FFF00') h$hue <- 0.5 h #> HSV('#00FFFF') h$saturation #> [1] 1 as.character(h) #> [1] "#00FFFF" HSVClass$from_rgb(c(1, 0, 0)) #> HSV('#FF0000') hues <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 13)[-13] rainbow_dots <- VGroup(lapply(hues, function(hh) Dot(radius = 0.35, color = as.character(HSV(c(hh, 0.7, 1)))))) plot(rainbow_dots$arrange_in_grid(rows = 2, buff = 0.3))

text: Give set_color(), set_fill() set_stroke() several colors fill stroke becomes linear gradient. gradient runs along mobject’s sheen_direction (UL default; change set_sheen_direction()).  groups, set_color_by_gradient() colors submobjects one along gradient, set_colors_by_radial_gradient() colors distance center.
code: a <- Square()$set_fill(c(RED, BLUE), opacity = 1) b <- Square(stroke_width = 0)$set_fill(c(RED, BLUE), opacity = 1)$set_sheen_direction(RIGHT) cc <- Circle()$set_fill(YELLOW, opacity = 1)$set_stroke(c(GREEN, PURPLE), width = 14) d <- Star(fill_opacity = 1)$set_color(c(PINK, YELLOW)) plot(VGroup(a, b, cc, d)$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.6)) a$get_fill_colors() #> [1] "#FC6255" "#58C4DD" a$get_sheen_direction() #> [1] -1  1  0 dots <- VGroup(lapply(1:16, function(i) Dot(radius = 0.18)))$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.15) dots$set_color_by_gradient(BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW) tiles <- VGroup(lapply(1:81, function(i) Square(side_length = 0.3, fill_opacity = 1, stroke_width = 1))) tiles$arrange_in_grid(rows = 9, buff = 0.04) tiles$set_colors_by_radial_gradient(radius = 1.5, inner_color = YELLOW, outer_color = RED) plot(VGroup(dots, tiles)$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.5))
