title: Mobjects and geometry
text: shift(...) moves vector (several vectors added). move_to(point_or_mobject, aligned_edge) puts center (given edge) point another mobject’s position. next_to(mobject_or_point, direction, buff, aligned_edge) places mobject beside another, buff units away. align_to(mobject_or_point, direction) lines one edge another mobject’s edge, without moving along axis. to_edge(edge, buff) to_corner(corner, buff) move frame’s edges corners.  orange square moved aligned_edge = DL, lower left corner, center, sits orange dot. align_to() lines edges. , bottom row copy top row whose members aligned group’s top edge:  frame stops losing things: buffers keep margin edge. standard values SMALL_BUFF (0.1), MED_SMALL_BUFF (0.25), MED_LARGE_BUFF (0.5) LARGE_BUFF (1); next_to() arrange() default DEFAULT_MOBJECT_TO_MOBJECT_BUFFER (0.25) to_edge() DEFAULT_MOBJECT_TO_EDGE_BUFFER (0.5).
code: box <- Square(side_length = 1.6, color = WHITE) pic <- VGroup(   box,   Circle(radius = 0.4, color = BLUE)$next_to(box, RIGHT),   Circle(radius = 0.4, color = GREEN)$next_to(box, UP, buff = 0.1),   Rectangle(width = 1.2, height = 0.5, color = YELLOW)$next_to(box, LEFT, aligned_edge = UP),   Triangle(color = RED)$scale(0.4)$next_to(box, DOWN, buff = 0.6),   Star(color = PURPLE, fill_opacity = 1)$scale(0.5)$to_corner(UL),   Text("to_edge(RIGHT)", font_size = 30)$to_edge(RIGHT),   Dot(color = ORANGE)$move_to(3 * LEFT + 2 * DOWN),   Square(side_length = 0.6, color = ORANGE)$move_to(3 * LEFT + 2 * DOWN, aligned_edge = DL) ) plot(pic) row <- VGroup(Square(1), Circle(radius = 0.8, color = BLUE), Rectangle(width = 1, height = 2.2, color = GREEN),               Triangle(color = YELLOW))$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.5)$shift(1.6 * UP) aligned <- row$copy()$shift(3.2 * DOWN) for (m in aligned$submobjects) m$align_to(aligned, UP) plot(VGroup(row, aligned, DashedLine(c(-4, aligned$get_top()[2], 0), c(4, aligned$get_top()[2], 0), color = GREY_B)))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: arrange(direction, buff, center) lines members group, next previous one; extra arguments aligned_edge go next_to(). arrange_in_grid() builds table: give rows cols, buff (one number, one columns one rows), alignments, flow_order ("rd" fills rows first, "dr" columns first).
code: numbered <- function(n) VGroup(lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {   VGroup(Square(side_length = 0.5 + 0.12 * (i %% 3), color = BLUE), Text(as.character(i), font_size = 30)) })) a <- numbered(5)$arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge = LEFT, buff = 0.1) b <- numbered(6)$arrange_in_grid(rows = 2, buff = c(0.3, 0.3)) d <- numbered(6)$arrange_in_grid(rows = 2, flow_order = "dr", buff = c(0.3, 0.3)) plot(VGroup(a, b, d)$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 1))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: match_width(), match_height(), match_x() match_y() copy size coordinate another mobject; surround() replace() fit one mobject another.
code: sq <- Square(side_length = 2)$shift(RIGHT) sq$get_center() #> [1] 1 0 0 sq$get_corner(UR) #> [1] 2 1 0 c(sq$get_top()[2], sq$get_bottom()[2], sq$get_left()[1], sq$get_right()[1]) #> [1]  1 -1  0  2 sq$get_critical_point(DL) #> [1]  0 -1  0 sq$get_x() #> [1] 1 c(sq$width, sq$height) #> [1] 2 2 sq$width <- 4      # width, height and depth can be set; the shape scales evenly sq$height #> [1] 4 sq$set_x(0)$get_center() #> [1] 0 0 0 Line(LEFT, RIGHT)$get_length() #> [1] 2 Circle()$get_arc_length() #> [1] 6.281205 zapsmall(Circle()$point_from_proportion(0.25)) #> [1] 0 1 0

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: scale(), rotate(), flip() stretch() work center default. Give about_point (point) about_edge (direction) keep another point fixed. pictures, gray outline original.  left right: scale(1.4), scale(1.4, about_edge = DL), rotate(PI / 6), rotate(PI / 6, about_point = <corner>), flip() (mirror image across vertical axis) stretch(1.6, 1). dimension argument stretch() counts 1, 1 x 2 y. rotate(angle, axis) turns counterclockwise axis (default). Rotations axes tilt mobject plane, matters 3D scenes.
code: ghost <- function(m) m$copy()$set_stroke(GREY_B, width = 2)$set_fill(opacity = 0) flag <- function() Polygon(c(0, -1, 0), c(0, 1, 0), c(1.2, 0.6, 0), c(0.3, 0.3, 0), c(0.3, -1, 0),                            color = YELLOW, fill_opacity = 0.6) s1 <- Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5) s2 <- Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5) s3 <- Square(color = GREEN, fill_opacity = 0.5) s4 <- Square(color = GREEN, fill_opacity = 0.5) f1 <- flag() c1 <- Circle(color = RED, fill_opacity = 0.5) panels <- VGroup(   VGroup(ghost(s1), s1$scale(1.4)),   VGroup(ghost(s2), s2$scale(1.4, about_edge = DL)),   VGroup(ghost(s3), s3$rotate(PI / 6)),   VGroup(ghost(s4), s4$rotate(PI / 6, about_point = s4$get_corner(DL))),   VGroup(ghost(f1), f1$flip(UP)),   VGroup(ghost(c1), c1$stretch(1.6, 1)) )$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.9) panels$width <- 13 plot(panels)

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: apply_function(func) sends every point function point, apply_matrix(matrix) multiplies every point 2 x 2 3 x 3 matrix (origin unless about_point given). apply_complex_function() takes function complex number. Extra curves (insert_n_curves()) keep bent shape smooth.  Matrices easier understand motion. ApplyMatrix() animates multiplication:
code: wave <- function(p) p + c(0, 0.3 * sin(2 * p[1]), 0) grid_lines <- function() {   g <- VGroup(c(lapply(seq(-1.5, 1.5, by = 0.5), function(k) Line(c(-1.5, k, 0), c(1.5, k, 0), color = BLUE)),                 lapply(seq(-1.5, 1.5, by = 0.5), function(k) Line(c(k, -1.5, 0), c(k, 1.5, 0), color = YELLOW))))   for (l in g$submobjects) l$insert_n_curves(16)   g } shear <- matrix(c(1, 0, 0.5, 1), 2) # (x, y) goes to (x + 0.5 y, y) bent <- VGroup(grid_lines(), grid_lines()$apply_function(wave), grid_lines()$apply_matrix(shear),                grid_lines()$apply_complex_function(function(z) z^2 / 3))$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.7) bent$width <- 13 plot(bent) ShearGrid <- R6::R6Class("ShearGrid", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     grid <- VGroup(c(lapply(-3:3, function(k) Line(c(-3, k, 0), c(3, k, 0), color = BLUE_D)),                      lapply(-3:3, function(k) Line(c(k, -3, 0), c(k, 3, 0), color = BLUE_D))))     sq <- Square(side_length = 1, color = YELLOW, fill_opacity = 0.6)$move_to(c(0.5, 0.5, 0))     self$add(grid, sq)     self$play(ApplyMatrix(matrix(c(1, 0, 1, 1), 2), VGroup(grid, sq)), run_time = 2)   }) )

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: VMobject fill (color opacity) stroke (color, width opacity). set_color() sets colors, set_fill() set_stroke() one , set_opacity() opacities. Stroke widths hundredths unit (default DEFAULT_STROKE_WIDTH 4). Every setter applies whole family unless family = FALSE.  Constructors take settings arguments: color, fill_color, fill_opacity, stroke_color, stroke_width stroke_opacity. set_style() sets several , get_style() reads , match_style() copies another mobject’s style. background stroke drawn behind fill. outlines text labels stay readable busy backgrounds:
code: styled <- VGroup(   Square()$set_color(BLUE),   Square()$set_fill(BLUE, opacity = 0.7),   Square()$set_fill(BLUE, opacity = 0.7)$set_stroke(YELLOW, width = 12),   Square(fill_opacity = 1, color = RED)$set_opacity(0.3),   Square(stroke_width = 0, fill_opacity = 1, color = GREEN) )$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.5) plot(styled) fancy <- Square()$set_style(fill_color = RED, fill_opacity = 0.5, stroke_color = BLUE, stroke_width = 8) str(fancy$get_style(simple = TRUE)) #> List of 5 #>  $ stroke_opacity: num 1 #>  $ stroke_width  : num 8 #>  $ fill_color    : chr "#FC6255" #>  $ fill_opacity  : num 0.5 #>  $ stroke_color  : chr "#58C4DD" Circle()$match_style(fancy)$get_stroke_width() #> [1] 8 fancy$get_fill_color() #> [1] "#FC6255" fancy$get_fill_opacity() #> [1] 0.5 outlined <- Text("outline", font_size = 72, color = YELLOW)$set_stroke(BLACK, width = 10, background = TRUE) plot(VGroup(Rectangle(width = 6, height = 1.6, color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 1), outlined))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Several colors make gradient; set_sheen() lightens toward one side. colors vignette details.
code: plot(VGroup(   Circle(fill_opacity = 1)$set_color(c(BLUE, GREEN)),   Star(fill_opacity = 1)$set_color(c(YELLOW, RED)),   Square(fill_opacity = 1, color = PURPLE)$set_sheen(0.7, UR),   VGroup(lapply(1:9, function(i) Dot(radius = 0.2)))$arrange(RIGHT)$set_color_by_gradient(BLUE, YELLOW) )$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.6))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Mobjects drawn order added, later ones cover earlier ones. higher z_index brings mobject front regardless:  Constructors also accept z_index = directly.
code: make_stack <- function() VGroup(   Square(color = RED, fill_opacity = 1),   Square(color = GREEN, fill_opacity = 1)$shift(0.6 * (RIGHT + DOWN)),   Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 1)$shift(1.2 * (RIGHT + DOWN)) ) default_order <- make_stack() raised <- make_stack() raised[1]$set_z_index(2) raised[2]$set_z_index(1) plot(VGroup(default_order, raised)$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 1.5))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: copy() returns independent deep copy, submobjects included. become() makes mobject take another’s points style keeping identity, animations updaters refer still work. save_state() stores snapshot restore() goes back . generate_target() makes copy $target modify; MoveToTarget() animation morphs mobject . animated version shows useful: target prepared first change happens one smooth move, Restore() animates back saved state.
code: original <- Square(color = BLUE) twin <- original$copy()$shift(RIGHT) original$get_center()       # unchanged #> [1] 0 0 0  morph <- Square() id <- morph$mob_id morph$become(Circle(color = RED)) morph$get_color() #> [1] "#FC6255" morph$mob_id == id          # still the same object #> [1] TRUE  s <- Square() s$save_state() s$shift(3 * RIGHT)$scale(0.5) s$restore()$get_center() #> [1] 0 0 0  invisible(s$generate_target()) s$target$shift(UP)$set_color(YELLOW) c(s$get_center()[2], s$target$get_center()[2]) #> [1] 0 1 StateAndTarget <- R6::R6Class("StateAndTarget", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     sq <- Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.6)$shift(3 * LEFT)     sq$save_state()     invisible(sq$generate_target())     sq$target$shift(6 * RIGHT)$scale(0.5)$rotate(PI / 4)$set_color(YELLOW)     ghost <- DashedVMobject(sq$target$copy()$set_fill(opacity = 0), num_dashes = 24)     self$add(ghost)     self$play(MoveToTarget(sq), run_time = 1.5)     self$play(sq$animate$shift(2 * UP), run_time = 0.8)     self$play(Restore(sq), run_time = 1.2)     self$add(Text("restored", font_size = 32)$next_to(sq, DOWN))     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: VGroup() groups VMobjects move style together; Group() groups mobjects, image shapes. accept mobjects lists mobjects, VGroup(lapply(...)) builds group loop. add() remove() change members afterwards.
code: g <- VGroup(Circle(), Square(), Triangle()) length(g) #> [1] 3 g$add(Star()) length(g) #> [1] 4 g$remove(g[1]) length(g) #> [1] 3 dots <- VGroup(lapply(1:5, function(i) Dot()))$arrange(RIGHT) length(dots) #> [1] 5 img <- ImageMobject(matrix(seq(0, 255, length.out = 64), 8, 8)) class(Group(img, Circle()))[1] #> [1] "Group"

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: g[] returns -th submobject, counting 1. vector indices returns group submobjects; negative indices drop members, R vectors. g[[]] also returns one submobject. length(g) counts submobjects, g$submobjects plain list, convenient loops. Indexing makes easy style parts group:
code: g <- VGroup(Circle(), Square(), Triangle(), Star()) class(g[2])[1] #> [1] "Square" class(g[2:3])[1] #> [1] "VGroup" length(g[-1]) #> [1] 3 class(g[[4]])[1] #> [1] "Star" for (m in g$submobjects) m$set_fill(opacity = 0.5) row <- VGroup(lapply(1:8, function(i) Square(side_length = 0.9)))$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.15) row[c(2, 4, 6, 8)]$set_fill(BLUE, opacity = 1) row[1]$set_color(YELLOW) row[[8]]$scale(0.6) plot(row)

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: VDict() VGroup whose members names. Index key (vector keys group), assign vd[key] <- mobject, use methods get(), add_key_value_pair(), remove_key() get_all_submobjects(). [[, character key returns field method one name, otherwise entry.
code: vd <- VDict(list(square = Square(color = BLUE), circle = Circle())) class(vd["square"])[1] #> [1] "Square" vd["triangle"] <- Triangle(color = GREEN) length(vd) #> [1] 3 vd$get("circle")$get_color() #> [1] "#FC6255" vd$remove_key("circle") length(vd) #> [1] 2 class(vd[c("square", "triangle")])[1] #> [1] "VGroup" plot(vd$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 1))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: section shows every shape. small helper lays catalog caption shape.
code: catalog <- function(items, cols = 4, font_size = 30, buff = c(0.7, 0.5)) {   cells <- VGroup(lapply(names(items), function(nm) {     VGroup(items[[nm]], Text(nm, font_size = font_size)$next_to(items[[nm]], DOWN, buff = 0.2))   }))   cells$arrange_in_grid(cols = cols, buff = buff)   cells$scale(min(1, 13.4 / cells$width, 7.6 / cells$height)) }

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Arc(radius, start_angle, angle, arc_center) sweeps angle radians counterclockwise start_angle. ArcBetweenPoints(start, end, angle) bends two points. Circle(radius) full arc; Ellipse(width, height) stretched circle. circle_from_three_points() CircleClass$from_three_points() find circle three points, $point_at_angle() gives point angle circle. Dot(point, radius) small filled circle; AnnotationDot() colored fill white stroke; LabeledDot(label) dot label inside (string typeset MathTex(), pass Text() mobject LaTeX available). CubicBezier(start_anchor, start_handle, end_handle, end_anchor) single Bezier curve.
code: plot(catalog(list(   "Arc" = Arc(radius = 1, start_angle = PI / 6, angle = 4 * PI / 3, color = BLUE),   "ArcBetweenPoints" = ArcBetweenPoints(LEFT, RIGHT, angle = PI / 2, color = GREEN),   "Circle" = Circle(radius = 1),   "Ellipse" = Ellipse(width = 2.4, height = 1.2, color = YELLOW),   "Dot" = Dot(radius = 0.2, color = WHITE),   "AnnotationDot" = AnnotationDot()$scale(2.5),   "LabeledDot" = LabeledDot(Text("A", font_size = 40, color = BLACK), color = YELLOW),   "CubicBezier" = CubicBezier(c(-1, -0.5, 0), c(-0.5, 1.5, 0), c(0.5, -1.5, 0), c(1, 0.5, 0), color = PINK) ))) through <- circle_from_three_points(LEFT, UP, c(1.5, 0.5, 0), color = TEAL) pts <- VGroup(Dot(LEFT), Dot(UP), Dot(c(1.5, 0.5, 0))) on_circle <- Dot(through$point_at_angle(-PI / 2), color = RED) plot(VGroup(through, pts, on_circle))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Sector(), AnnularSector() Annulus() filled default. ArcPolygon() joins vertices arcs (one angle radius , list settings arc_config); ArcPolygonFromArcs() joins given arcs straight segments meet. keep arcs submobjects ($arcs), drawn style; arcs carry orange outline first shape, one arc Reuleaux triangle visible (red) stroke.
code: p3 <- list(c(-1, -0.6, 0), c(1, -0.6, 0), c(0, 1.1, 0)) arc_poly <- ArcPolygon(p3[[1]], p3[[2]], p3[[3]], arc_config = list(angle = PI / 3, color = ORANGE),                        fill_color = ORANGE, fill_opacity = 0.3, stroke_width = 0) a <- c(-1, -0.6, 0) b <- c(1, -0.6, 0) cc <- c(0, sqrt(3) - 0.6, 0) reuleaux <- ArcPolygonFromArcs(   ArcBetweenPoints(a, b, radius = 2, stroke_width = 0),   ArcBetweenPoints(b, cc, radius = 2, stroke_width = 0),   ArcBetweenPoints(cc, a, radius = 2, stroke_color = RED),   color = PURPLE, fill_opacity = 1 ) plot(catalog(list(   "Sector" = Sector(radius = 1.2, angle = PI / 3, color = BLUE),   "AnnularSector" = AnnularSector(inner_radius = 0.6, outer_radius = 1.2, angle = 2 * PI / 3, color = GREEN),   "Annulus" = Annulus(inner_radius = 0.6, outer_radius = 1.1, color = RED),   "ArcPolygon" = arc_poly,   "ArcPolygonFromArcs" = reuleaux ), cols = 5))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Line(start, end, buff, path_arc) accepts points mobjects start end (starts edges), buff shortens ends. Lines helpers geometry: TangentLine(vmob, alpha, length) touches curve proportion alpha length, Elbow(width, angle) small corner mark used right angles.
code: curve <- Circle(radius = 0.9, color = GREY_B) plot(catalog(list(   "Line" = Line(c(-1, -0.5, 0), c(1, 0.5, 0), color = BLUE),   "Line(path_arc = )" = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, path_arc = PI / 2, color = GREEN),   "DashedLine" = DashedLine(LEFT, RIGHT, color = YELLOW, dash_length = 0.15),   "TangentLine" = VGroup(curve, TangentLine(curve, alpha = 0.125, length = 2.2, color = RED)),   "Elbow" = Elbow(width = 0.8, angle = PI / 4, color = PINK) ), cols = 5)) ln <- Line(ORIGIN, c(3, 4, 0)) c(ln$get_length(), ln$get_angle() / DEGREES, ln$get_slope()) #> [1]  5.000000 53.130102  1.333333 ln$get_vector() #> [1] 3 4 0 ln$get_unit_vector() #> [1] 0.6 0.8 0.0 ln$put_start_and_end_on(LEFT, RIGHT)$get_length() #> [1] 2 ln$set_length(5)$get_length() #> [1] 5 Line(Circle()$shift(2 * LEFT), Circle()$shift(2 * RIGHT))$get_start() # starts at the edge #> [1] -1  0  0

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Arrow(start, end, buff) stops buff short end points (0.25 default) keeps tip proportion short. Vector(direction) starts origin. line arc can get tip add_tip(), start add_tip(at_start = TRUE); get_tip(), get_tips(), has_tip() pop_tips() manage . tip shape class generator passed tip_shape (tip_shape_start tip_shape_end double arrows). base class tips ArrowTipClass, class anything can carry tips TipableVMobjectClass.
code: plot(catalog(list(   "Arrow" = Arrow(LEFT, RIGHT, color = BLUE),   "DoubleArrow" = DoubleArrow(LEFT, RIGHT, color = GREEN),   "Vector" = Vector(c(1.2, 0.8, 0), color = YELLOW),   "CurvedArrow" = CurvedArrow(LEFT, RIGHT, color = RED),   "CurvedDoubleArrow" = CurvedDoubleArrow(LEFT, RIGHT, color = PINK),   "Line + add_tip()" = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color = TEAL)$add_tip() ), cols = 3)) tips <- c("ArrowTriangleTipClass", "ArrowTriangleFilledTipClass", "ArrowCircleTipClass",           "ArrowCircleFilledTipClass", "ArrowSquareTipClass", "ArrowSquareFilledTipClass", "StealthTipClass") tip_rows <- VGroup(lapply(seq_along(tips), function(i) {   y <- 3.4 - 0.85 * i   arrow <- Arrow(c(0.5, y, 0), c(3.5, y, 0), tip_shape = get(tips[i]), color = YELLOW)   VGroup(Text(tips[i], font_size = 30)$next_to(arrow, LEFT, buff = 0.4), arrow) })) plot(tip_rows$center()) arrow <- Arrow(LEFT, RIGHT) arrow$has_tip() #> [1] TRUE zapsmall(arrow$get_tip()$tip_angle) #> [1] -3.766828e-16 arrow$get_tip()$length #> [1] 0.35

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Angle(line1, line2) marks angle two lines meet. Choose four angles quadrant, take reflex angle other_angle = TRUE, mark dot right angle elbow. RightAngle() elbow version; angle_from_three_points(, B, C) (AngleClass$from_three_points()) builds angle B, get_value() reads .  TangentialArc(line1, line2, radius, corner) arc given radius tangent lines, rounded corner :
code: make_lines <- function() VGroup(Line(ORIGIN, 1.6 * RIGHT), Line(ORIGIN, rotate_vector(1.6 * RIGHT, PI / 3))) l1 <- make_lines() l2 <- make_lines() l3 <- VGroup(Line(1.2 * LEFT, 1.2 * RIGHT), Line(rotate_vector(1.2 * LEFT, PI / 3), rotate_vector(1.2 * RIGHT, PI / 3))) l4 <- make_lines() l5 <- VGroup(Line(ORIGIN, 1.6 * RIGHT), Line(ORIGIN, 1.6 * UP)) plot(catalog(list(   "Angle" = VGroup(l1, Angle(l1[1], l1[2], color = YELLOW)),   "other_angle = TRUE" = VGroup(l2, Angle(l2[1], l2[2], other_angle = TRUE, radius = 0.4, color = GREEN)),   "quadrant = c(-1, -1)" = VGroup(l3, Angle(l3[1], l3[2], quadrant = c(-1, -1), color = RED)),   "dot = TRUE" = VGroup(l4, Angle(l4[1], l4[2], dot = TRUE, color = BLUE)),   "RightAngle" = VGroup(l5, RightAngle(l5[1], l5[2], length = 0.4, color = PINK)) ), cols = 5)) angle_from_three_points(RIGHT, ORIGIN, UP)$get_value(degrees = TRUE) #> [1] 90 Angle(l1[1], l1[2])$get_value() #> [1] 1.047198 h <- Line(c(-4, -2, 0), c(4, -2, 0), color = GREY_B) v <- Line(c(0, -3.5, 0), c(0, 3, 0), color = GREY_B) plot(VGroup(h, v,             TangentialArc(h, v, radius = 1.5, color = YELLOW, stroke_width = 6),             TangentialArc(h, v, radius = 1, corner = c(-1, 1), color = RED, stroke_width = 6)))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Polygon(...) takes vertices separate points one matrix. Polygram(...) takes vertex groups (one matrix ) draws closed path, can several pieces. RegularPolygon(n) RegularPolygram(num_vertices, density) (star polygon connects every densityth vertex); Triangle() RegularPolygon(3). Star(n, outer_radius, inner_radius, density) star outline. Rectangle(width, height, grid_xstep, grid_ystep) can draw grid inside; Square(side_length); RoundedRectangle(corner_radius). get_vertices() returns corners, round_corners(radius) rounds :
code: plot(catalog(list(   "Polygon" = Polygon(c(-1, -0.8, 0), c(1, -0.8, 0), c(1.2, 0.5, 0), c(0, 1, 0), c(-1.2, 0.3, 0), color = BLUE),   "Triangle" = Triangle(color = GREEN),   "Square" = Square(side_length = 1.6, color = YELLOW),   "Rectangle" = Rectangle(width = 2.2, height = 1.2, color = RED),   "RegularPolygon(6)" = RegularPolygon(6, color = TEAL),   "RegularPolygram(7, 3)" = RegularPolygram(7, density = 3, color = PURPLE),   "Star(5)" = Star(5, color = GOLD),   "RoundedRectangle" = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius = 0.3, width = 2.2, height = 1.3, color = PINK) ))) hexagon <- RegularPolygon(6) nrow(hexagon$get_vertices()) #> [1] 6 two_parts <- Polygram(rbind(c(-1, 0, 0), c(0, 1, 0), c(1, 0, 0)),                       rbind(c(-1, -0.4, 0), c(1, -0.4, 0), c(0, -1.4, 0)), color = ORANGE) plot(catalog(list(   "Polygram (2 groups)" = two_parts,   "round_corners(0.3)" = Triangle(color = BLUE)$scale(1.2)$round_corners(radius = 0.3),   "Rectangle with grid" = Rectangle(width = 2.4, height = 1.6, grid_xstep = 0.4, grid_ystep = 0.4, color = GREEN),   "Star(7, density = 3)" = Star(7, outer_radius = 1, density = 3, color = YELLOW) )))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Cutout(main_shape, ...) punches shapes main one, holes show behind. ConvexHull(...) smallest convex polygon around set points.
code: stripes <- VGroup(lapply(1:6, function(i) {   Rectangle(width = 3, height = 0.5, stroke_width = 0, fill_opacity = 1, fill_color = c(RED, YELLOW)[i %% 2 + 1]) }))$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0) holes <- Cutout(Square(side_length = 3), Circle(radius = 0.5)$shift(0.6 * UL),                 Triangle()$scale(0.6)$shift(0.6 * DR), fill_opacity = 1, color = BLUE, stroke_width = 0) set.seed(4) cloud <- cbind(runif(20, -1.5, 1.5), runif(20, -1.2, 1.2), 0) hull <- ConvexHull(cloud, color = YELLOW) cloud_dots <- VGroup(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cloud)), function(i) Dot(cloud[i, ], radius = 0.05))) plot(VGroup(VGroup(stripes, holes),             VGroup(hull, cloud_dots))$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 1.5))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: SurroundingRectangle() frames mobject (optional rounded corners), BackgroundRectangle() puts translucent rectangle behind , Underline() draws line Cross() crosses (makes plain X without mobject).
code: framed <- Text("frame", font_size = 44) backed <- Text("back", font_size = 44) underlined <- Text("under", font_size = 44) crossed <- Text("wrong", font_size = 44) plot(catalog(list(   "SurroundingRectangle" = VGroup(framed, SurroundingRectangle(framed, corner_radius = 0.1)),   "BackgroundRectangle" = VGroup(Square(side_length = 1, color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 1)$shift(0.4 * UP),                                  BackgroundRectangle(backed, fill_opacity = 0.8), backed),   "Underline" = VGroup(underlined, Underline(underlined, color = YELLOW)),   "Cross" = VGroup(crossed, Cross(crossed)) ), cols = 4, font_size = 26))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Union(), Intersection(), Difference() Exclusion() combine shapes way drawing program . need suggested ‘polyclip’ package. result new VMobject made straight segments (curves sampled finely), takes usual style arguments.  Union() Intersection() take two shapes; Difference(subject, clip) removes clip subject, Exclusion() keeps exactly one two covers.
code: sq <- Square(color = RED, fill_opacity = 0.5)$move_to(0.4 * LEFT) ci <- Circle(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5)$move_to(0.4 * RIGHT + 0.4 * UP) plot(catalog(list(   "inputs" = VGroup(sq$copy(), ci$copy()),   "Union" = Union(sq, ci, color = GREEN, fill_opacity = 1),   "Intersection" = Intersection(sq, ci, color = YELLOW, fill_opacity = 1),   "Difference" = Difference(sq, ci, color = PINK, fill_opacity = 1),   "Exclusion" = Exclusion(sq, ci, color = TEAL, fill_opacity = 1) ), cols = 5))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Brace(mobject, direction) draws curly brace along one side mobject. put_at_tip() places another mobject tip, get_text() / get_tex() make label . BraceLabel() makes brace label one go (label constructor MathTex() default; BraceText() uses Text()). BraceBetweenPoints() spans two points, ArcBrace() follows arc.
code: rect <- Rectangle(width = 3, height = 1.5, color = BLUE) b_down <- Brace(rect, DOWN) b_left <- Brace(rect, LEFT, color = YELLOW) width_label <- Text("width", font_size = 30) b_down$put_at_tip(width_label) with_braces <- VGroup(rect, b_down, b_left, width_label) p1 <- c(-1.5, -1, 0) p2 <- c(1, 1, 0) between <- VGroup(Dot(p1), Dot(p2), BraceBetweenPoints(p1, p2, color = GREEN)) arc <- Arc(radius = 1.5, start_angle = PI / 6, angle = 2 * PI / 3, color = RED) side_sq <- Square(side_length = 1.6, color = TEAL) plot(catalog(list(   "Brace + put_at_tip()" = with_braces,   "BraceText" = VGroup(side_sq, BraceText(side_sq, "side", font_size = 30)),   "BraceBetweenPoints" = between,   "ArcBrace" = VGroup(arc, ArcBrace(arc)) ), cols = 4, font_size = 26)) plot(BraceLabel(Line(2 * LEFT, 2 * RIGHT), "x^2 + y^2", brace_direction = UP))

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: Label() label background box frame. LabeledLine() LabeledArrow() put label label_position (proportion length), LabeledPolygram() puts polygon’s pole inaccessibility, interior point farthest edges (see polylabel() Math utility functions). string label typeset MathTex(); Text() mobject works without LaTeX. label_config, box_config frame_config style parts. Fills use nonzero winding rule, SVG upstream: ring inside another hole vertices run opposite way, inner ring polygram listed clockwise.
code: ring <- list(rbind(c(-2, -1.2, 0), c(2, -1.2, 0), c(2, 1.2, 0), c(-2, 1.2, 0)),     # counterclockwise              rbind(c(-1.6, -0.8, 0), c(-1.6, 0.8, 0), c(-0.2, 0.8, 0), c(-0.2, -0.8, 0))) # clockwise: a hole plot(catalog(list(   "Label" = Label(Text("Label", font_size = 36), box_config = list(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.8)),   "LabeledLine" = LabeledLine(Text("0.8", font_size = 28), label_position = 0.8,                               start = c(-1.5, -0.7, 0), end = c(1.5, 0.7, 0), color = YELLOW),   "LabeledArrow" = LabeledArrow(Text("force", font_size = 28), start = c(-1.5, 0, 0), end = c(1.5, 0, 0),                                 color = GREEN),   "LabeledPolygram" = LabeledPolygram(ring[[1]], ring[[2]], label = Text("pole", font_size = 28),                                       color = RED, fill_opacity = 0.3) ), cols = 4, font_size = 26))

what: Dashed paths, pieces and screen shapes

text: path can drawn setting points VMobject() . set_points_as_corners(points) joins points straight segments. set_points_smoothly(points) passes smooth spline . start_new_path(point) starts (new) piece point; add_line_to(), add_cubic_bezier_curve_to(handle1, handle2, anchor), add_quadratic_bezier_curve_to(handle, anchor) add_smooth_curve_to(point) continue ; close_path() closes . make_smooth() make_jagged() change corners , set_points() append_points() take raw Bezier control points.  path can animated like built shape. Create() draws along points:
code: zigzag <- rbind(c(-1.5, -1, 0), c(-0.75, 1, 0), c(0, -1, 0), c(0.75, 1, 0), c(1.5, -1, 0)) corners <- VMobject(color = BLUE)$set_points_as_corners(zigzag) smooth <- VMobject(color = GREEN)$set_points_smoothly(zigzag)  drawn <- VMobject(color = YELLOW, fill_opacity = 0.3) drawn$start_new_path(c(-1.5, -1, 0)) drawn$add_line_to(c(-1.5, 0.5, 0)) drawn$add_cubic_bezier_curve_to(c(-1, 1.5, 0), c(0, 1.5, 0), c(0.5, 0.5, 0)) drawn$add_quadratic_bezier_curve_to(c(1.5, 0.5, 0), c(1.5, -1, 0)) drawn$close_path()  two_pieces <- VMobject(color = RED) two_pieces$start_new_path(c(-1.5, 0.5, 0)) two_pieces$add_smooth_curve_to(c(0, 1.2, 0)) two_pieces$add_smooth_curve_to(c(1.5, 0.5, 0)) two_pieces$start_new_path(c(-1.5, -0.8, 0)) two_pieces$add_line_to(c(1.5, -0.8, 0))  plot(catalog(list(   "set_points_as_corners" = corners,   "set_points_smoothly" = smooth,   "lines and curves" = drawn,   "start_new_path" = two_pieces ))) drawn$get_num_curves() #> [1] 4 drawn$is_closed() #> [1] TRUE length(two_pieces$get_subpaths()) #> [1] 2 DrawSpiral <- R6::R6Class("DrawSpiral", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     t <- seq(0, 4 * PI, length.out = 120)     spiral <- VMobject(color = YELLOW, stroke_width = 6)     spiral$set_points_smoothly(cbind(0.25 * t * cos(t), 0.25 * t * sin(t), 0))     spiral$set_color(c(BLUE, YELLOW))     self$play(Create(spiral), run_time = 2)   }) )

title: Mobjects and geometry
text: reusable shape, subclass mobject class R6. usual pattern class generator plus constructor function, exactly manimR’s shapes built. Set fields calling super$initialize(), parent initializer calls generate_points(). VMobject whose points generated parameters, rose curve: group subclass assembles mobjects, labeled pie chart. methods available like , scales, moves animates one mobject:  Subclasses take part everything shown vignette: positioning, styling, copying, grouping every animation.
code: RoseClass <- R6::R6Class("Rose", inherit = VMobjectClass,   public = list(     petals = 5,     radius = 1.5,     initialize = function(petals = 5, radius = 1.5, ...) {       self$petals <- petals       self$radius <- radius       super$initialize(...)     },     generate_points = function() {       t <- seq(0, TAU, length.out = 40 * self$petals)       r <- self$radius * cos(self$petals * t)       self$set_points_smoothly(cbind(r * cos(t), r * sin(t), 0))     }   ) ) Rose <- function(...) RoseClass$new(...)  rose <- Rose(petals = 5, color = PINK, fill_opacity = 0.4) class(rose) #> [1] "Rose"     "VMobject" "Mobject"  "R6" PieChartClass <- R6::R6Class("PieChart", inherit = VGroupClass,   public = list(     values = NULL,     initialize = function(values, colors = NULL, radius = 1.5, ...) {       super$initialize(...)       self$values <- values       colors <- colors %||% color_gradient(c(BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW, RED), length(values))       angles <- TAU * values / sum(values)       starts <- cumsum(c(0, angles))[seq_along(values)]       for (i in seq_along(values)) {         self$add(Sector(radius = radius, start_angle = starts[i], angle = angles[i],                         color = colors[i], fill_opacity = 1, stroke_width = 2, stroke_color = BLACK))       }     },     share = function(i) self$values[i] / sum(self$values)   ) ) PieChart <- function(...) PieChartClass$new(...)  pie <- PieChart(c(3, 2, 4, 1)) length(pie) #> [1] 4 pie$share(3) #> [1] 0.4 plot(VGroup(rose, pie)$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 1.5))

file.path(tempdir(), "manim-videos") dir.create(video_dir, showWarnings = FALSE) addResourcePath("videos", video_dir)  ui <- fluidPage(   titlePanel("manimR in Shiny"),   sidebarLayout(     sidebarPanel(       sliderInput("n", "Number of sides", min = 3, max = 12, value = 5),       selectInput("color", "Color", c("BLUE", "RED", "GREEN", "YELLOW")),       actionButton("go", "Render")     ),     mainPanel(uiOutput("video"))   ) )  server <- function(input, output, session) {   output$video <- renderUI({     req(input$go)     n <- isolate(input$n)     color <- get(isolate(input$color), envir = asNamespace("manimR"))     scene <- manim_scene(function(self) {       shape <- RegularPolygon(n = n)$scale(2)$set_fill(color, opacity = 0.5)       self$play(Create(shape))       self$play(Rotate(shape, angle = PI))     }, name = "PolygonScene")     file <- file.path(video_dir, sprintf("polygon-%d.mp4", input$go))     withProgress(message = "Rendering", {       render(scene, quality = "l", output_file = file, media_dir = tempdir())     })     tags$video(src = file.path("videos", basename(file)), type = "video/mp4",                controls = NA, autoplay = NA, loop = NA, muted = NA, width = "100%")   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server) output$frame <- renderImage({   png <- render(scene, quality = "m", format = "png", media_dir = tempdir())   list(src = unclass(png), contentType = "image/png", width = "100%") }, deleteFile = FALSE)

title: Text, math and tables
text: Text() draws string system font. main arguments font_size (48 default), color, font (family name; "sans", "serif" "mono" work everywhere), weight slant.  Weights slants strings, available constants names upstream manim: NORMAL, ITALIC OBLIQUE slant, THIN, ULTRALIGHT, LIGHT, SEMILIGHT, BOOK, NORMAL, MEDIUM, SEMIBOLD, BOLD, ULTRABOLD, HEAVY ULTRAHEAVY weight (see ?font_constants). font lacks weight uses closest one .  TextClass$font_list() lists font families installed system: font file installed can used register_font(), makes file available family name returns name. looks file given, assets/fonts/ fonts/ working directory. font file works, including one already installed, runnable example (family name depends system):  Upstream manim’s register_font() context manager forgets font block ends; manimR font stays registered rest R session.
code: lines <- VGroup(   Text("The default font at size 48"),   Text("serif at size 36", font = "serif", font_size = 36),   Text("mono and bold", font = "mono", weight = BOLD),   Text("sans, italic and yellow", font = "sans", slant = ITALIC, color = YELLOW) ) plot(lines$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.4)) c(NORMAL, ITALIC, OBLIQUE) #> [1] "NORMAL"  "ITALIC"  "OBLIQUE" weights <- c(THIN, ULTRALIGHT, LIGHT, SEMILIGHT, BOOK, NORMAL, MEDIUM, SEMIBOLD, BOLD, ULTRABOLD, HEAVY, ULTRAHEAVY) samples <- VGroup(lapply(weights, function(w) Text(w, weight = w, font_size = 40))) plot(samples$arrange_in_grid(rows = 4, cols = 3, buff = c(0.8, 0.4))) head(TextClass$font_list()) #> [1] "Bitstream Charter"    "C059"                 "Courier"              #> [4] "D050000L"             "DejaVu Math TeX Gyre" "DejaVu Sans" family <- register_font("fonts/MyFont-Regular.ttf") Text("Hello", font = family) font_file <- systemfonts::match_fonts("serif")$path family <- register_font(font_file) plot(Text(paste("Registered font:", family), font = family))

code: greeting <- Text("Hello world") length(greeting$submobjects) #> [1] 10 greeting[1]$set_color(RED) greeting$get_part_by_text("world")$set_color(YELLOW) greeting$font_size <- 96 greeting$font_size #> [1] 96 plot(greeting)

title: Text, math and tables
text: Five arguments style parts text. takes named list whose names substrings (every occurrence styled) slices "[2:5]": t2c: colors. t2f: fonts. t2s: slants. t2w: weights. t2g: gradients, given vectors colors. Slices follow upstream manim Python: count 0 exclude end, "[2:5]" third fifth characters. differs R indexing text[1], counts 1. gradient colors whole text gradient.
code: parts <- VGroup(   Text("Hello world, hello R", t2c = list(world = YELLOW, R = BLUE), t2w = list(Hello = BOLD),        t2s = list(world = ITALIC), t2f = list(R = "mono")),   Text("0123456789", t2c = list("[2:5]" = RED)),   Text("a gradient on one word", t2g = list(gradient = c(TEAL, PURPLE))),   Text("Rainbow text", gradient = c(RED, YELLOW, GREEN, BLUE)) ) plot(parts$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.4))

code: TextAnimation <- R6::R6Class("TextAnimation", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     title <- Text("Text in motion", font_size = 72)     self$play(Write(title))     self$play(title$get_part_by_text("motion")$animate$set_color(YELLOW))     self$play(title$animate$scale(0.6)$to_edge(UP))     body <- Paragraph("Each glyph is a submobject,", "so parts can move on their own.",                       alignment = "center", font_size = 36)     self$play(FadeIn(body, shift = UP, lag_ratio = 0.02))     self$wait(0.5)   }) )

text: Tex() typesets LaTeX text mode MathTex() math mode (inside align* environment). need LaTeX installation dvisvgm. R strings backslash written twice, "\\frac{1}{2}"; raw strings r"(\frac{1}{2})" avoid doubling.
code: plot(VGroup(   Tex("Hello \\LaTeX, with \\textbf{bold} and \\emph{emphasis}"),   MathTex(r"(e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0)"),   MathTex(r"(\int_0^1 x^2 \, dx = \frac{1}{3})", color = YELLOW, font_size = 60) )$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.5))

title: Text, math and tables
text: Every string passed MathTex() (Tex()) becomes one submobject, eq[3] b^2 part. Double braces split single string way: MathTex("{{^2}} + {{b^2}}") parts ^2, + b^2. Methods look parts LaTeX string : set_color_by_tex(tex, color) set_opacity_by_tex(tex, opacity). get_part_by_tex(tex), first part string, get_parts_by_tex(tex), group . index_of_part_by_tex(tex), position among submobjects.  substrings_to_isolate splits every occurrence given substrings, can colored even inside single string, tex_to_color_map isolates colors substrings one step. arg_separator text inserted strings (space MathTex(), nothing Tex()), tex_environment LaTeX environment ("align*" MathTex(), "center" Tex()). SingleStringMathTex() typesets one string without splitting.
code: eq <- MathTex("a^2", "+", "b^2", "=", "c^2") eq$font_size <- 96 length(eq$submobjects) #> [1] 5 eq[3]$set_color(BLUE) eq$set_color_by_tex("c^2", YELLOW) eq$get_part_by_tex("+")$set_color(RED) eq$index_of_part_by_tex("=") #> [1] 4 plot(eq) plot(VGroup(   MathTex("(x + 1)^2 = x^2 + 2x + 1", substrings_to_isolate = "x")$set_color_by_tex("x", BLUE),   MathTex(r"(\alpha + \beta = \gamma)", tex_to_color_map = list("\\alpha" = RED, "\\beta" = GREEN)),   SingleStringMathTex(r"(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n^2} = \frac{\pi^2}{6})") )$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.5)$scale(1.3))

text: BulletedList() typesets one bulleted item per string; fade_all_but() dims every item except one. Title() places title top frame underline (include_underline, match_underline_width_to_text).

title: Text, math and tables
text: LaTeX document around expression comes TexTemplate(). Add packages add_to_preamble() commands \begin{document} add_to_document(); tex_compiler output_format choose compiler ("latex" ".dvi", "xelatex" ".xdv", "lualatex" ".pdf"). Pass template tex_template one mobject, make default everything manim_config(tex_template = ...). TexTemplateClass$from_file() reads whole template .tex file.  TexTemplateLibrary() returns ready made templates (default, threeb1b, ctex simple), TexFontTemplates() returns fifty templates switch font text math. Upstream manim stores class attributes, TexTemplateLibrary.ctex; R functions return fresh list time, written TexTemplateLibrary()$ctex, changing one template affect another. font templates need extra LaTeX packages (one uses frcursive mathastext, part TeX Live).  tex_to_svg_file() function underneath: compiles expression returns path SVG file, SVGMobject() can load. file draws black, give imported shapes fill_color.
code: script <- TexTemplate() script$add_to_preamble("\\usepackage{mathrsfs}") plot(MathTex(r"(\mathscr{L}\{f\}(s) = \int_0^\infty f(t) e^{-st} \, dt)", tex_template = script, font_size = 80)) names(TexTemplateLibrary()) #> [1] "default"  "threeb1b" "ctex"     "simple" length(TexFontTemplates()) #> [1] 52 TexFontTemplates()$french_cursive$description #> [1] "French Cursive (Euler Greek)" cursive <- TexFontTemplates()$french_cursive plot(Tex("Handwritten $x^2 + y^2 = 1$", tex_template = cursive, font_size = 72)) svg <- tex_to_svg_file(r"(\sqrt{2})", environment = "align*") basename(svg) #> [1] "24fb166be7fce66f.svg" plot(SVGMobject(svg, fill_color = WHITE, height = 2))

title: Text, math and tables
text: Typst modern typesetting system single small compiler. Typst() takes Typst markup MathTypst() math expression without $ signs. Install typst command line compiler, point manimR manim_config(typst = "/path//typst").  Parts selected select(). MathTypst(), {{ content : label }} names part {{ content }} numbers , select("lhs") select(1) return groups glyphs. Unlike upstream manim, numeric keys count 1. general Typst markup, parts marked ordinary Typst labels, #box[body] <label>. typst_preamble adds Typst code (#set rules) body.  typst_to_svg_file() compiles Typst code SVG file returns path, like tex_to_svg_file() LaTeX.
code: plot(VGroup(   Typst("*Hello* from _Typst!_", font_size = 72),   MathTypst("integral_0^1 x^2 dif x = 1/3", color = YELLOW, font_size = 60) )$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.6)) eq <- MathTypst("{{ a^2 + b^2 : lhs }} = {{ c^2 }}", font_size = 96) eq$select("lhs")$set_color(BLUE) eq$select(1)$set_color(YELLOW) fancy <- Typst("#box[Labeled] <word> text in italics", typst_preamble = "#set text(style: \"italic\")") fancy$select("word")$set_color(ORANGE) plot(VGroup(eq, fancy)$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.6)) basename(typst_to_svg_file("$sum_(k=1)^n k = n(n+1)/2$")) #> [1] "d39970d512f28aca.svg"

title: Text, math and tables
text: Code() shows highlighted source code, string (code_string) file (code_file, language guessed extension). R Python highlighted; languages shown one color, warning. listing made Text() lines monospaced font, LaTeX needed. formatter_style: one built styles (CodeClass$get_styles_list()), named list colors like entries CodeClass$get_pygments_style("monokai"). add_line_numbers line_numbers_from: line numbers. background: "rectangle" "window" (three buttons), styled background_config. paragraph_config: arguments Text() lines, font_size.  parts fields: code_lines (VGroup one Text() per line), line_numbers background. makes easy point line:

title: Text, math and tables
text: DecimalNumber() shows number can change later set_value(); get_value() reads increment_value() adds . Integer() decimal places. formatting arguments : num_decimal_places: digits decimal point. include_sign: always show sign. group_with_commas: thousands separators (default). unit: LaTeX appended number, raised starts ^. show_ellipsis: append ellipsis. edge_to_fix: edge stays place value changes. mob_class: constructor used character, MathTex default.  mob_class = Text digits come system fonts, number works without LaTeX:  Variable() combines label, equals sign number driven value tracker. Numbers follow changing values, Variable(), covered Updaters value trackers; counting animations ChangeDecimalToValue() ChangingDecimal() Animations.
code: numbers <- VGroup(   DecimalNumber(1234567.891, num_decimal_places = 3),   DecimalNumber(-3.2, include_sign = TRUE, unit = "^\\circ"),   DecimalNumber(42.5, unit = "\\%"),   DecimalNumber(3.14159, num_decimal_places = 4, show_ellipsis = TRUE),   Integer(-17),   DecimalNumber(1 + 2i) ) plot(numbers$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.25)$scale(1.5)) count <- Integer(7) count$increment_value(3) count$get_value() #> [1] 10 price <- DecimalNumber(19.99, mob_class = Text, font_size = 96, color = GREEN) price$set_value(24.5) price$get_value() #> [1] 24.5 plot(price)

title: Text, math and tables
text: Matrix() lays entries grid brackets. accepts R matrix, data frame, list rows. Entries go element_to_mobject (MathTex() default, strings may contain LaTeX), brackets LaTeX delimiters, matrices need LaTeX. left_bracket right_bracket: "[" "]" default; "(", "\\{" "|" also work. v_buff h_buff: spacing rows columns. element_alignment_corner: corner entry aligned grid. DecimalMatrix(), IntegerMatrix() MobjectMatrix() use DecimalNumber(), Integer() arbitrary mobjects entries.  accessors get_rows(), get_columns() get_entries() (groups, indexed 1) get_brackets(); set_row_colors() set_column_colors() color whole rows columns, add_background_to_entries() puts dark rectangle behind every entry.  matrix_to_tex_string() writes R matrix LaTeX array, matrix_to_mobject() typesets one piece (without separate entries Matrix()). get_det_text() builds “det( ) = value” decoration around matrix; add matrix separately.  Matrices animate like group. column highlighted entries move.
code: plain <- Matrix(list(list(2, "\\pi"), list(-1, "\\sqrt{2}"))) decimal <- DecimalMatrix(rbind(c(3.14159, 2.71828), c(1.41421, 1.73205)),                          element_to_mobject_config = list(num_decimal_places = 2)) integer <- IntegerMatrix(rbind(c(1, 2), c(3, 4)), left_bracket = "(", right_bracket = ")") shapes <- MobjectMatrix(list(list(Circle(radius = 0.3), Square(side_length = 0.6)),                              list(Triangle()$scale(0.35), Star(outer_radius = 0.35)))) plot(VGroup(plain, decimal, integer, shapes)$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.6)$scale_to_fit_width(13)) m <- Matrix(rbind(c(1, 2, 3), c(4, 5, 6), c(7, 8, 9))) m$set_column_colors(RED, GREEN, BLUE) m$get_rows()[2]$set_color(YELLOW) m$get_entries()[9]$set_color(WHITE) box <- SurroundingRectangle(m$get_columns()[1]) plot(VGroup(m, box)$scale(1.8)) matrix_to_tex_string(matrix(1:4, 2)) #> [1] "\\left[ \\begin{array}{cc}1 & 3 \\\\ 2 & 4\\end{array} \\right]" a <- Matrix(rbind(c(2, 0), c(-1, 1))) det <- get_det_text(a, determinant = 2, initial_scale_factor = 1) plot(VGroup(VGroup(a, det)$shift(LEFT * 3), matrix_to_mobject(rbind(c(1, 0), c(0, 1)))$shift(RIGHT * 3))$scale(1.6)) MatrixAnimation <- R6::R6Class("MatrixAnimation", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     m <- IntegerMatrix(rbind(c(1, 2), c(3, 4)), h_buff = 1.5)$scale(1.5)     self$play(Write(m))     column <- m$get_columns()[2]     box <- SurroundingRectangle(column, color = YELLOW)     self$play(Create(box))     self$play(column$animate$set_color(YELLOW))     self$play(Swap(m$get_entries()[2], m$get_entries()[4]))     self$wait(0.5)   }) )

title: Text, math and tables
text: Table() arranges entries grid lines cells. accepts R matrix, data frame list rows; entries go Paragraph(), plain strings need LaTeX. row_labels, col_labels top_left_entry: lists mobjects labeling rows columns, corner . include_outer_lines (default) include_inner_lines. v_buff h_buff: spacing; line_config: arguments lines, stroke_width color. element_to_mobject element_to_mobject_config: entries built, arrange_in_grid_config layout. Positions table c(row, column), counted 1 labels included, row column labels c(2, 2) first entry. add_highlighted_cell(pos, color) puts colored background behind cell; get_highlighted_cell() returns background without adding , get_cell() cell’s outline polygon.  accessors return groups indexed 1: get_rows(), get_columns(), get_entries() (entries, one pos), get_entries_without_labels() (, positions skip labels), get_row_labels(), get_col_labels(), get_labels(), get_horizontal_lines() get_vertical_lines(). set_row_colors() set_column_colors() color whole rows columns, add_background_to_entries() puts rectangle behind entry.  MobjectTable() takes mobjects entries. MathTable(), IntegerTable() DecimalTable() typeset entries MathTex(), Integer() DecimalNumber(), need LaTeX.   tab$create() returns animation draws lines, entries labels, highlighted cells. arguments choose animations used part (line_animation, element_animation, label_animation, entry_animation) lag_ratio.
code: df <- data.frame(model = c("linear", "quadratic"), rmse = c("2.31", "1.07"), r2 = c("0.81", "0.96")) tab <- Table(df,   col_labels = list(Text("model"), Text("RMSE"), Text("R squared")),   include_outer_lines = TRUE,   line_config = list(stroke_width = 2, color = GREY_B) ) tab$add_highlighted_cell(c(3, 2), color = GREEN) tab$get_col_labels()$set_color(YELLOW) outline <- tab$get_cell(c(3, 3), color = RED, stroke_width = 6) glow <- tab$get_highlighted_cell(c(2, 1), color = PURPLE) plot(VGroup(glow, tab, outline)$scale(1.1)) grid <- Table(list(c("a", "b", "c"), c("d", "e", "f")),               row_labels = list(Text("row 1"), Text("row 2"))) length(grid$get_entries()$submobjects) #> [1] 8 length(grid$get_entries_without_labels()$submobjects) #> [1] 6 length(grid$get_horizontal_lines()$submobjects) #> [1] 1 grid$set_column_colors(WHITE, BLUE, GREEN, ORANGE) grid$get_entries_without_labels(c(2, 3))$set_color(RED) plot(grid$scale(1.4)) shapes <- MobjectTable(list(   list(Circle(radius = 0.4, color = BLUE), Square(side_length = 0.8, color = GREEN)),   list(Triangle(color = RED)$scale(0.45), Star(outer_radius = 0.45, color = YELLOW)) )) plot(shapes$scale(1.5)) addition <- MathTable(list(list("+", 0, 1), list(0, 0, 1), list(1, 1, 2)), include_outer_lines = TRUE) counts <- IntegerTable(rbind(c(12, 7), c(3, 25)), col_labels = list(Text("yes"), Text("no")),                        row_labels = list(Text("A"), Text("B"))) rates <- DecimalTable(rbind(c(0.125, 0.5), c(0.875, 1)),                       element_to_mobject_config = list(num_decimal_places = 3)) rates$set_row_colors(GREEN, ORANGE) plot(VGroup(addition, counts, rates)$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 0.7)$scale_to_fit_width(13)) TableCreate <- R6::R6Class("TableCreate", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     tab <- Table(list(c("1", "2", "3"), c("4", "5", "6")),                  col_labels = list(Text("x"), Text("y"), Text("z")), title: Text, math and tables
text: MathTex() one submobject per part, equations can written, recolored rearranged step step. Write() draws equation, TransformMatchingTex() moves part part LaTeX string next equation, fading rest. Animations vignette describes options. Parts can also animated , example highlight term rewriting :
code: SolveEquation <- R6::R6Class("SolveEquation", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     step1 <- MathTex("2", "x", "+", "3", "=", "11")$scale(2)     step2 <- MathTex("2", "x", "=", "11", "-", "3")$scale(2)     step3 <- MathTex("2", "x", "=", "8")$scale(2)     step4 <- MathTex("x", "=", "4")$scale(2)     self$play(Write(step1))     self$play(step1$animate$set_color_by_tex("x", YELLOW))     for (step in list(step2, step3, step4)) step$set_color_by_tex("x", YELLOW)     self$play(TransformMatchingTex(step1, step2, path_arc = PI / 2))     self$play(TransformMatchingTex(step2, step3))     self$play(TransformMatchingTex(step3, step4))     self$play(Circumscribe(step4))     self$wait(0.5)   }) ) HighlightTerms <- R6::R6Class("HighlightTerms", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     eq <- MathTex("(a + b)^2", "=", "a^2", "+", "2ab", "+", "b^2", font_size = 80)     self$add(eq)     self$play(Indicate(eq[5]))     self$play(eq[3]$animate$set_color(BLUE), eq[7]$animate$set_color(GREEN))     brace <- Brace(eq[5], DOWN)     note <- Text("the cross term", font_size = 32)$next_to(brace, DOWN)     self$play(GrowFromCenter(brace), FadeIn(note, shift = UP))     self$wait(0.5)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: mob$add_updater(f) attaches function f(m), called every frame mobject . label updater keeps dot, follows dot every animation without animated . add_updater() returns mobject, chains. Two arguments control : call_updater = TRUE runs function right away, puts label place first frame, index inserts updater position list updaters (run order). mob$get_updaters() returns list.
code: FollowTheDot <- R6::R6Class("FollowTheDot", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     dot <- Dot(LEFT * 4, radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)     label <- Text("follow me", font_size = 32)     label$add_updater(function(m) m$next_to(dot, UP))     self$add(dot, label)     self$play(dot$animate$shift(RIGHT * 4 + UP * 1.5))     self$play(dot$animate$shift(RIGHT * 4 + DOWN * 3), run_time = 1.5)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: function argument named dt, time based updater, called f(m, dt) time seconds since previous frame. Multiplying rate dt gives motion constant speed depend frame rate. argument called dt: name, number arguments, tells manimR pass time. scene time based updaters keeps rendering new frames self$wait(), scene without just repeats still frame. self$pause() always holds still frame run updaters.
code: DtUpdater <- R6::R6Class("DtUpdater", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     square <- Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(LEFT * 3)     square$add_updater(function(m, dt) m$rotate(PI / 2 * dt))     dot <- Dot(RIGHT * 1, radius = 0.15, color = ORANGE)     dot$add_updater(function(m, dt) m$shift(RIGHT * 1.5 * dt))     self$add(square, dot)     self$wait(2)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: mob$remove_updater(f) removes one updater. function object added, store function variable first. mob$clear_updaters() removes updaters mobject submobjects. mob$suspend_updating() pauses updaters without removing , mob$resume_updating() turns back (runs ). label stops following dot updaters suspended jumps back resume. updater removed good. Animations also suspend updaters: animation plays, updaters mobject animates paused (resumed end), updater animation fight mobject. Pass suspend_mobject_updating = FALSE animation keep running.
code: dot <- Dot() drift <- function(m, dt) m$shift(RIGHT * dt) dot$add_updater(drift) length(dot$get_updaters()) #> [1] 1 dot$has_time_based_updater() #> [1] TRUE dot$remove_updater(drift) length(dot$get_updaters()) #> [1] 0 SuspendResume <- R6::R6Class("SuspendResume", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     dot <- Dot(LEFT * 3, radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)     label <- Text("label", font_size = 32)     stay_above <- function(m) m$next_to(dot, UP)     label$add_updater(stay_above, call_updater = TRUE)     self$add(dot, label)     self$play(dot$animate$shift(RIGHT * 2))     label$suspend_updating()     self$play(dot$animate$shift(DOWN * 1.5))     label$resume_updating()     self$wait(0.3)     label$remove_updater(stay_above)     self$play(dot$animate$shift(RIGHT * 3))     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: ValueTracker invisible mobject stores one number. Read get_value() change set_value() increment_value(). mobject, $animate animates number smoothly current value new one. usual pattern : keep state tracker, give mobjects updaters read , animate tracker. pointer number follow tracker along number line. DecimalNumber() normally typesets digits LaTeX; mob_class = Text uses system fonts instead, example runs without LaTeX. Setting value directly (tracker$set_value(-1) ) jumps; updaters pick new value next frame. Arithmetic tracker works value returns new tracker +, -, *, / ^, plain value comparisons: Upstream manim’s place operators tracker += 1 R equivalent; use tracker$increment_value(1). ComplexValueTracker stores complex number, handy points plane: Re() Im() value coordinates.
code: tracker <- ValueTracker(1) tracker$get_value() #> [1] 1 tracker$set_value(3) tracker$increment_value(0.5) tracker$get_value() #> [1] 3.5 TrackerNumberLine <- R6::R6Class("TrackerNumberLine", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     line <- NumberLine(x_range = c(-5, 5, 1), length = 10)     tracker <- ValueTracker(0)     pointer <- Triangle(color = YELLOW, fill_opacity = 1)$scale(0.15)$rotate(PI)     pointer$add_updater(function(m) m$next_to(line$n2p(tracker$get_value()), UP), call_updater = TRUE)     number <- DecimalNumber(0, num_decimal_places = 2, mob_class = Text, font_size = 36)     number$add_updater(function(m) m$set_value(tracker$get_value())$next_to(pointer, UP), call_updater = TRUE)     self$add(line, pointer, number)     self$play(tracker$animate$set_value(4))     self$play(tracker$animate$increment_value(-6.5), run_time = 1.5)     tracker$set_value(-1)     self$wait(0.3)     self$play(tracker$animate(rate_func = there_and_back)$set_value(2), run_time = 1.5)     self$wait(0.3)   }) ) a <- ValueTracker(2) (a * 3)$get_value() #> [1] 6 a > 1 #> [1] TRUE ComplexTracker <- R6::R6Class("ComplexTracker", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     plane <- NumberPlane(x_range = c(-4, 4, 1), y_range = c(-3, 3, 1))     z <- ComplexValueTracker(-3 + 2i)     dot <- Dot(radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)     dot$add_updater(function(m) m$move_to(c(Re(z$get_value()), Im(z$get_value()), 0)), call_updater = TRUE)     self$add(plane, dot)     self$play(z$animate$set_value(3 - 1i))     self$play(z$animate$set_value(z$get_value() * 1i), run_time = 1.5)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: always_redraw(f) takes function arguments builds mobject, calls , adds updater rebuilds mobject scratch every frame. simplest way draw something depends moving mobjects, line two dots. Rebuilding slower adjusting existing mobject, prefer plain updater method call move_to() next_to() enough.
code: AlwaysRedraw <- R6::R6Class("AlwaysRedraw", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     a <- Dot(LEFT * 3 + DOWN, radius = 0.15, color = BLUE)     b <- Dot(RIGHT * 3 + UP, radius = 0.15, color = ORANGE)     link <- always_redraw(function() Line(a$get_center(), b$get_center(), color = YELLOW))     brace <- always_redraw(function() Brace(link, direction = DOWN, color = GREY))     self$add(link, brace, a, b)     self$play(a$animate$shift(UP * 2.5 + RIGHT), b$animate$shift(DOWN * 2))     self$play(Rotate(b, angle = PI / 2, about_point = ORIGIN), run_time = 1.5)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: always(mob$method, ...) calls method arguments every frame. always(label$next_to, dot, ) shorthand label$add_updater(function(m) m$next_to(dot, )). mob$always$method(...) upstream manim’s syntax (label.always.next_to(dot, )), also calls method right away. f_always(mob$method, ...) passes functions arguments; called every frame produce argument. Use argument changes, point read tracker. Named arguments passed .

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: always_shift(mob, direction, rate) moves mobject rate units per second always_rotate(mob, rate, ...) turns rate radians per second (arguments about_point go rotate()). add time based updater return mobject.
code: AlwaysHelpers <- R6::R6Class("AlwaysHelpers", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     x <- ValueTracker(-4)     dot <- Dot(radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)     f_always(dot$move_to, function() c(x$get_value(), -2, 0))     label <- Text("f_always", font_size = 28)     always(label$next_to, dot, UP)     square <- Square(side_length = 1.2, color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 3 + UP * 1.5)     always_rotate(square, rate = PI / 2)     star <- Star(outer_radius = 0.5, color = ORANGE)$shift(RIGHT * 1 + UP * 1.5)     always_shift(star, direction = RIGHT, rate = 1)     tag <- Text("always_shift", font_size = 24)     tag$always$next_to(star, DOWN)     self$add(dot, label, square, star, tag)     self$play(x$animate$set_value(4), run_time = 2)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: turn_animation_into_updater(anim) plays animation updater mobject instead self$play(), runs alongside whatever else happens, starting delay seconds. cycle = TRUE, shortcut cycle_animation(anim), restarts whenever ends. scene keeps playing self$wait().
code: AnimationUpdater <- R6::R6Class("AnimationUpdater", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     once <- Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(LEFT * 3)     looping <- Circle(color = ORANGE)$shift(RIGHT * 3)     turn_animation_into_updater(Rotate(once, angle = PI / 4, run_time = 1), delay = 0.5)     cycle_animation(Indicate(looping, run_time = 1))     self$add(once, looping)     self$wait(2)     self$wait(0.5)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: Three animations run function every frame, play, work like temporary updaters: UpdateFromFunc(mob, f) calls f(mob). UpdateFromAlphaFunc(mob, f) calls f(mob, alpha), alpha going 0 1 animation’s rate function. Make f set properties absolute values, since runs every frame. MaintainPositionRelativeTo(mob, tracked) keeps mob offset tracked animation started.
code: UpdateFromFuncExample <- R6::R6Class("UpdateFromFuncExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     dot <- Dot(LEFT * 4 + UP * 1.5, radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)     label <- Text("UpdateFromFunc", font_size = 28)$next_to(dot, UP)     square <- Square(color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 3 + DOWN * 1.5)     box <- Square(side_length = 0.8, color = ORANGE)$shift(RIGHT * 1 + DOWN * 1.5)     tag <- Text("MaintainPositionRelativeTo", font_size = 24)$next_to(box, UP)     self$add(dot, label, square, box, tag)     self$play(       dot$animate$shift(RIGHT * 8),       UpdateFromFunc(label, function(m) m$next_to(dot, UP)),       UpdateFromAlphaFunc(square, function(m, alpha) m$set_fill(BLUE, opacity = alpha)),       box$animate$shift(RIGHT * 3),       MaintainPositionRelativeTo(tag, box),       run_time = 2     )     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: TracedPath(f) line grows every frame point returned f(), function arguments dot$get_center. dissipating_time, oldest part disappears many seconds, leaves short tail. AnimatedBoundary(vmob) draws outline around VMobject keeps redrawing cycling colors, cycle_rate cycles per second. mobjects built time based updaters: add scene run .
code: AnimatedBoundaryExample <- R6::R6Class("AnimatedBoundaryExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     word <- Text("Animated boundary", font_size = 60)     boundary <- AnimatedBoundary(word, colors = c(RED, GREEN, BLUE), cycle_rate = 3)     self$add(word, boundary)     self$wait(1)     self$play(word$animate$set_color(YELLOW))     self$wait(1)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: scene can updaters : self$add_updater(f) registers function f(dt) time step , called per frame mobject updaters; self$remove_updater(f) removes . Use state belongs scene rather one mobject. self$wait_until(stop_condition, max_time = 60) waits function stop_condition() returns TRUE, checking every frame, max_time seconds passed. self$wait(max_time, stop_condition = stop_condition). Use length wait depends updaters . comet moves along circle reading angle scene updater advances, leaves dissipating trail, scene waits gone around one half times.
code: Comet <- R6::R6Class("Comet", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     angle <- ValueTracker(0)     self$add_updater(function(dt) angle$increment_value(PI * dt))     comet <- Dot(radius = 0.12, color = YELLOW)     comet$add_updater(function(m) {       m$move_to(2.5 * c(cos(angle$get_value()), sin(angle$get_value()), 0))     }, call_updater = TRUE)     trail <- TracedPath(comet$get_center, stroke_color = YELLOW, stroke_width = 4, dissipating_time = 0.6)     self$add(Dot(radius = 0.3, color = ORANGE), comet, trail)     self$wait_until(function() angle$get_value() >= 3 * PI, max_time = 5)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: DecimalNumber() (Integer() whole numbers) can updated set_value(), redraws digits keeping edge given edge_to_fix place. updater gives live readout. formatting arguments include num_decimal_places, include_sign, group_with_commas, unit (LaTeX appended number, "^\\circ"), show_ellipsis. examples section use default LaTeX digits, need LaTeX installation.

what: A dot on a graph with a live label
title: Updaters and value trackers
text: classic: value tracker x, dot redrawn graph x, number showing sin(x) rides along dot.
code: GraphDotLabel <- R6::R6Class("GraphDotLabel", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     axes <- Axes(x_range = c(-4, 4, 1), y_range = c(-1.5, 1.5, 0.5), x_length = 11, y_length = 5)     graph <- axes$plot(function(x) sin(x), color = BLUE)     x <- ValueTracker(-4)     dot <- always_redraw(function() Dot(axes$i2gp(x$get_value(), graph), radius = 0.1, color = YELLOW))     value <- DecimalNumber(sin(-4), num_decimal_places = 2, include_sign = TRUE, font_size = 36)     value$add_updater(function(m) m$set_value(sin(x$get_value()))$next_to(dot, UP), call_updater = TRUE)     self$add(axes, graph, dot, value)     self$play(x$animate$set_value(4), run_time = 3, rate_func = linear)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: Variable(value, label) packages pattern: label, equals sign number driven tracker, stored $tracker. Animate tracker change number. var_type = "integer" shows whole numbers. count number without tracker, use ChangeDecimalToValue() ChangingDecimal() animations Animations.
code: VariableExample <- R6::R6Class("VariableExample", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     x <- Variable(0.5, "x", num_decimal_places = 3)$shift(UP)     n <- Variable(1, "n", var_type = "integer")$next_to(x, DOWN, aligned_edge = LEFT)     self$add(x, n)     self$play(x$tracker$animate$set_value(2.718), n$tracker$animate$set_value(100), run_time = 2)     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: time based updater turns hand constant rate, quarter turn per second, long scene runs.
code: Clock <- R6::R6Class("Clock", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     face <- Circle(radius = 2.5, color = WHITE)     ticks <- VGroup(lapply(0:11, function(i) {       Line(UP * 2.2, UP * 2.5)$rotate(-i * TAU / 12, about_point = ORIGIN)     }))     hand <- Line(ORIGIN, UP * 2, color = RED, stroke_width = 6)     hand$add_updater(function(m, dt) m$rotate(-TAU / 4 * dt, about_point = ORIGIN))     self$add(face, ticks, hand, Dot(radius = 0.1))     self$wait(3)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: wheel rolls along ground: updater shifts forward turns matching angle (distance radius), traced path follows point rim, drawing cycloid. scene waits wheel reaches right side, removes updater stops.
code: RollingCircle <- R6::R6Class("RollingCircle", inherit = Scene,   public = list(construct = function() {     r <- 0.7     speed <- 2.5     ground <- Line(LEFT * 7, RIGHT * 7, color = GREY)$shift(DOWN * 2)     circle <- Circle(radius = r, color = BLUE)$move_to(c(-5.5, -2 + r, 0))     spoke <- Line(circle$get_center(), circle$get_bottom(), color = BLUE)     rim_point <- Dot(circle$get_bottom(), radius = 0.08, color = YELLOW)     wheel <- VGroup(circle, spoke, rim_point)     wheel$add_updater(function(m, dt) {       center <- circle$get_center()       m$rotate(-speed * dt / r, about_point = center)       m$shift(RIGHT * speed * dt)     })     trace <- TracedPath(rim_point$get_center, stroke_color = YELLOW, stroke_width = 3)     self$add(ground, wheel, trace)     self$wait_until(function() circle$get_x() >= 5.5, max_time = 6)     wheel$clear_updaters()     self$wait(0.3)   }) )

title: Updaters and value trackers
text: ChangeSpeed() plays animation faster slower parts. Ordinary updaters keep pace; updater added change_speed_add_updater(mob, f) speeds slows together animation. See Animations example.

title: Math and utility functions
text: direction constants unit vectors. Add scale build points: 2 * RIGHT + point (2, 1, 0). UL, UR, DL DR diagonal corners (UL = + LEFT), unit vectors. point screen; default rotation axis everywhere.
code: rbind(ORIGIN, UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, IN, OUT) #>        [,1] [,2] [,3] #> ORIGIN    0    0    0 #> UP        0    1    0 #> DOWN      0   -1    0 #> LEFT     -1    0    0 #> RIGHT     1    0    0 #> IN        0    0   -1 #> OUT       0    0    1 rbind(UL, UR, DL, DR) #>    [,1] [,2] [,3] #> UL   -1    1    0 #> UR    1    1    0 #> DL   -1   -1    0 #> DR    1   -1    0 rbind(X_AXIS, Y_AXIS, Z_AXIS) #>        [,1] [,2] [,3] #> X_AXIS    1    0    0 #> Y_AXIS    0    1    0 #> Z_AXIS    0    0    1 2 * RIGHT + UP #> [1] 2 1 0 dirs <- list(RIGHT = RIGHT, UR = UR, UP = UP, UL = UL, LEFT = LEFT, DL = DL, DOWN = DOWN, DR = DR) cols <- color_gradient(c(BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW, RED), length(dirs)) pic <- VGroup() for (i in seq_along(dirs)) {   d <- dirs[[i]]   pic$add(Arrow(ORIGIN, 2 * d, buff = 0, color = cols[i]))   pic$add(Text(names(dirs)[i], font_size = 26, color = cols[i])$move_to(2.6 * d)) } plot(pic)

title: Math and utility functions
text: font constants strings Text() accepts slant weight, Text("Hi", weight = BOLD) reads like upstream code. LineJointType CapStyleType name values VMobject’s joint_type cap_style: corners thick stroke joined open ends capped.
code: c(NORMAL, ITALIC, OBLIQUE) #> [1] "NORMAL"  "ITALIC"  "OBLIQUE" c(THIN, ULTRALIGHT, LIGHT, SEMILIGHT, BOOK, NORMAL, MEDIUM, SEMIBOLD, BOLD, ULTRABOLD, HEAVY, ULTRAHEAVY) #>  [1] "THIN"       "ULTRALIGHT" "LIGHT"      "SEMILIGHT"  "BOOK"       #>  [6] "NORMAL"     "MEDIUM"     "SEMIBOLD"   "BOLD"       "ULTRABOLD"  #> [11] "HEAVY"      "ULTRAHEAVY" str(LineJointType) #> List of 4 #>  $ AUTO : chr "auto" #>  $ ROUND: chr "round" #>  $ BEVEL: chr "bevel" #>  $ MITER: chr "miter" str(CapStyleType) #> List of 4 #>  $ AUTO  : chr "auto" #>  $ ROUND : chr "round" #>  $ BUTT  : chr "butt" #>  $ SQUARE: chr "square" zigzag <- rbind(c(-1, -0.6, 0), c(-0.3, 0.6, 0), c(0.3, -0.6, 0), c(1, 0.6, 0)) joints <- VGroup() for (j in c("round", "bevel", "miter")) {   line <- VMobject(stroke_width = 30, color = BLUE, joint_type = LineJointType[[toupper(j)]])   line$set_points_as_corners(zigzag)   joints$add(VGroup(line, Text(paste("joint:", j), font_size = 24)$next_to(line, DOWN))) } caps <- VGroup() for (cp in c("butt", "round", "square")) {   line <- Line(LEFT, RIGHT, stroke_width = 40, color = ORANGE, cap_style = CapStyleType[[toupper(cp)]])   caps$add(VGroup(line, Text(paste("cap:", cp), font_size = 24)$next_to(line, DOWN))) } plot(VGroup(joints$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 1), caps$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 1.2))$arrange(DOWN, buff = 0.8))

title: Math and utility functions

title: Math and utility functions
text: angle_of_vector() gives angle vector plane, measured counterclockwise RIGHT; angle_between_vectors() gives unsigned angle two vectors space. rotation_matrix(angle, axis) returns 3 x 3 matrix rotation axis (right hand rule), rotation_about_z() special case z axis, rotate_vector() applies rotation vector. z_to_vector() returns rotation takes z axis given direction, 3D mobjects oriented. compass_directions(n) spreads n unit vectors evenly around circle, regular_vertices(n) returns vertices regular polygon angle started . picture puts together: fan vectors made rotate_vector(), pentagon regular_vertices() eight compass_directions().
code: angle_of_vector(UP) / DEGREES #> [1] 90 angle_of_vector(DL) / DEGREES #> [1] -135 angle_between_vectors(RIGHT, UR) / DEGREES #> [1] 45 zapsmall(rotation_matrix(PI / 2, OUT)) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]    0   -1    0 #> [2,]    1    0    0 #> [3,]    0    0    1 zapsmall(rotation_about_z(PI / 2)) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]    0   -1    0 #> [2,]    1    0    0 #> [3,]    0    0    1 zapsmall(rotate_vector(RIGHT, PI / 2)) #> [1] 0 1 0 zapsmall(rotate_vector(RIGHT, PI / 2, axis = UP)) # around the y axis #> [1]  0  0 -1 zapsmall(z_to_vector(RIGHT)) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]    0    0    1 #> [2,]    0    1    0 #> [3,]   -1    0    0 zapsmall(z_to_vector(RIGHT) %*% OUT) #>      [,1] #> [1,]    1 #> [2,]    0 #> [3,]    0 zapsmall(compass_directions(4)) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]    1    0    0 #> [2,]    0    1    0 #> [3,]   -1    0    0 #> [4,]    0   -1    0 rv <- regular_vertices(5, radius = 2) zapsmall(rv$vertices) #>           [,1]      [,2] [,3] #> [1,]  0.000000  2.000000    0 #> [2,] -1.902113  0.618034    0 #> [3,] -1.175571 -1.618034    0 #> [4,]  1.175571 -1.618034    0 #> [5,]  1.902113  0.618034    0 rv$start_angle / DEGREES #> [1] 90 v <- c(2, 0.6, 0) fan <- VGroup(lapply(0:5, function(k) {   Arrow(ORIGIN, rotate_vector(v, k * TAU / 12), buff = 0, color = interpolate_color(BLUE, YELLOW, k / 5)) })) pent <- regular_vertices(5, radius = 1.6)$vertices pentagon <- VGroup(Polygon(pent, color = GREEN), # a matrix of vertices works too                    VGroup(lapply(1:5, function(i) Dot(pent[i, ], color = YELLOW)))) comp <- compass_directions(8, start_vect = RIGHT) compass <- VGroup(lapply(1:8, function(i) Arrow(ORIGIN, 1.5 * comp[i, ], buff = 0, color = RED))) plot(VGroup(fan, pentagon, compass)$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 1))

title: Math and utility functions
text: plane doubles complex plane: complex_to_R3() turns x + yi c(x, y, 0) R3_to_complex() goes back. complex_func_to_R3_func() wraps function complex number function point, apply_function() expects. grid lines bent z^2 / 2. line gets extra curves first (insert_n_curves()) bent copy stays smooth.
code: complex_to_R3(1 + 2i) #> [1] 1 2 0 R3_to_complex(c(3, -1, 0)) #> [1] 3-1i square_it <- complex_func_to_R3_func(function(z) z^2) square_it(c(1, 1, 0)) # (1 + i)^2 = 2i #> [1] 0 2 0 make_grid <- function() {   g <- VGroup()   for (k in seq(-1.5, 1.5, by = 0.5)) {     g$add(Line(c(-1.5, k, 0), c(1.5, k, 0), color = BLUE, stroke_width = 2))     g$add(Line(c(k, -1.5, 0), c(k, 1.5, 0), color = YELLOW, stroke_width = 2))   }   for (line in g$submobjects) line$insert_n_curves(20)   g } half_square <- complex_func_to_R3_func(function(z) z^2 / 2) before <- make_grid() after <- make_grid()$apply_function(half_square) plot(VGroup(before, after)$arrange(RIGHT, buff = 1.5))

title: Math and utility functions
text: line_intersection() intersects two lines plane, given two points. find_intersection() takes point direction line instead, handles many pairs given matrices. perpendicular_bisector() returns two end points perpendicular bisector segment.
code: l1 <- rbind(c(-3, -1, 0), c(1, 2, 0)) l2 <- rbind(c(-3, 2, 0), c(0, -1.5, 0)) p <- line_intersection(l1, l2) p #> [1] -1.434783  0.173913  0.000000 find_intersection(c(0, 0, 0), c(1, 1, 0), c(2, 0, 0), c(-1, 1, 0)) #> [1] 1 1 0 find_intersection(rbind(ORIGIN, ORIGIN), rbind(RIGHT, UR),                   rbind(c(2, 1, 0), c(0, 3, 0)), rbind(DOWN, RIGHT)) # one pair per row #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]    2    0    0 #> [2,]    3    3    0 seg <- rbind(c(1.5, -1, 0), c(4, 1, 0)) pb <- perpendicular_bisector(seg) pb #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] 0.75  2.5    0 #> [2,] 4.75 -2.5    0 plot(VGroup(   Line(l1[1, ], l1[2, ], color = BLUE),   Line(l2[1, ], l2[2, ], color = GREEN),   Dot(p, color = YELLOW, radius = 0.12),   Line(seg[1, ], seg[2, ], color = RED),   Dot(seg[1, ], color = RED), Dot(seg[2, ], color = RED),   DashedLine(pb[1, ], pb[2, ], color = WHITE),   Dot(midpoint(seg[1, ], seg[2, ]), color = WHITE) ))

title: Math and utility functions
text: interpolate(start, end, alpha) blends linearly works numbers, points whole matrices points. inverse_interpolate() answers reverse question, match_interpolate() maps value one range another, mid() midpoint. integer_interpolate() splits progress value index fraction left ; DrawBorderThenFill(), example, uses split progress outline stage fill stage. index 0 based, upstream’s: add 1 using index R vector. sigmoid() logistic function, binary_search() inverts monotone function numerically (returning NULL target reach), clip_value() clamps number range. called clip_value() exported clip() mask graphics::clip(); upstream’s choose() simply base::choose().

text: partial_bezier_points(points, , b) returns control points part curve t = t = b. split_bezier() cuts one t stacks halves; subdivide_bezier() cuts n equal parameter pieces; bezier_remap() subdivides path several curves requested number curves, two paths made compatible Transform. picture shows control polygon (dashed), whole curve (blue), part t = 0.25 t = 0.75 (yellow) points subdivide_bezier() cuts three (red).

title: Math and utility functions
text: get_smooth_cubic_bezier_handle_points() computes handles join list anchors smooth spline (set_points_smoothly() make_smooth() use). returns first second handle curve. Interleaving anchors handles gives points VMobject:  is_closed() tells whether spline ends starts, decides whether smoothing also wraps around start point. reproduces upstream’s test exactly, including quirk: tolerance uses signed first coordinate, spline starting negative coordinate never counts closed.
code: anchors <- rbind(c(-4, -1, 0), c(-2, 1.5, 0), c(0, -1, 0), c(2, 1, 0), c(4, -1.5, 0)) h <- get_smooth_cubic_bezier_handle_points(anchors) h #> $h1 #>            [,1]       [,2] [,3] #> [1,] -3.3333333  0.4136905    0 #> [2,] -1.3333333  1.1726190    0 #> [3,]  0.6666667 -1.1041667    0 #> [4,]  2.6666667  1.2440476    0 #>  #> $h2 #>            [,1]       [,2] [,3] #> [1,] -2.6666667  1.8273810    0 #> [2,] -0.6666667 -0.8958333    0 #> [3,]  1.3333333  0.7559524    0 #> [4,]  3.3333333 -0.1279762    0 n <- nrow(anchors) - 1 pts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {   rbind(anchors[i, ], h$h1[i, ], h$h2[i, ], anchors[i + 1, ]) })) spline <- VMobject(color = YELLOW, stroke_width = 6) spline$set_points(pts) handles <- VGroup(lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {   VGroup(Line(anchors[i, ], h$h1[i, ], color = GREY_B, stroke_width = 2),          Line(h$h2[i, ], anchors[i + 1, ], color = GREY_B, stroke_width = 2),          Dot(h$h1[i, ], color = GREY_B, radius = 0.05), Dot(h$h2[i, ], color = GREY_B, radius = 0.05)) })) plot(VGroup(handles, spline, VGroup(lapply(1:5, function(i) Dot(anchors[i, ], color = RED))))) is_closed(rbind(c(0, 0, 0), c(1, 2, 0), c(0, 0, 0))) #> [1] TRUE is_closed(rbind(c(1, 1, 0), c(1, 2, 0), c(1.5, 1, 0))) #> [1] FALSE is_closed(rbind(c(-1, 0, 0), c(1, 2, 0), c(-1, 0, 0))) # the quirk #> [1] TRUE

code: rf <- rate_functions[setdiff(names(rate_functions),                              c("unit_interval", "zero", "not_quite_there", "squish_rate_func"))] names(rf)[names(rf) == "smooth"] <- "smooth_rate" rf[["not_quite_there()"]] <- not_quite_there() rf[["squish_rate_func(smooth_rate)"]] <- squish_rate_func(smooth_rate) t <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 201) op <- par(mfrow = c(8, 6), mar = c(1.2, 1.4, 1.6, 0.4), mgp = c(2, 0.35, 0), tcl = -0.2,           cex.main = 0.68, cex.axis = 0.6, font.main = 1) for (nm in names(rf)) {   y <- vapply(t, rf[[nm]], numeric(1))   plot(t, y, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#236B8E", main = nm, xlab = "", ylab = "",        ylim = range(0, 1, y))   abline(h = c(0, 1), col = "grey70", lty = 3) } par(op)
